findings.paper_title: Treasury Management Performance Report 2026-27 - Quarter 2
findings.headline: Treasury risks for inflation, interest rates and refinancing are recorded as having increased in the current economic environment
findings.detail: The paper says the risk register has been updated and that the top five risks are shown in Appendix 8. The Appendix 8 extract itself is not included in the text provided.
findings.matters: Councils that report rising treasury risk are a useful comparison for finance officers reviewing their own registers.
findings.figures: None given
findings.quote: The risks relating to inflation, interest rates and refinancing have all increased due to the current economic environment

findings.paper_title: Treasury Management Performance Report 2026-27 - Quarter 2
findings.headline: Liability benchmark estimates the Council is under-borrowed by £69.420m, with an average duration of 26 years
findings.detail: The paper says the benchmark is the optimum level of borrowing for the Council, and that the gap can guide how much and for how long to borrow. The paper gives this as a figure at 31 March 2026 in the text and as a figure at 31 March 2027 in Appendix 1.
findings.matters: A finance director deciding when to replace maturing loans, or whether to take new borrowing, will use this gap as the reference point.
findings.figures: £69.420m under-borrowed at 31 March 2026 (text); £69.42m at 31 March 2027 (Appendix 1); average duration 26 years
findings.quote: this is currently estimated to be £69.420m at 31 st March 2026

findings.paper_title: Treasury Management Performance Report 2026-27 - Quarter 2
findings.headline: Capital Financing Requirement forecast to rise to £464.627m by 31st March 2027, from £385.872m at 31 March 2026
findings.detail: The forecast is based on the capital programme agreed in February 2026, including fully and provisionally approved schemes. The paper says the gap between the CFR and the borrowing portfolio reflects internal balances being used in place of borrowing.
findings.matters: A rising CFR with internal balances covering the gap is a funding pattern lenders and finance directors track when assessing future borrowing need.
findings.figures: £464.627m forecast at 31st March 2027; £385.872m actual at 31 March 2026; borrowing portfolio £294.482m
findings.quote: is forecast to be £464.627m on 31st March 2027

findings.paper_title: Treasury Management Performance Report 2026-27 - Quarter 2
findings.headline: Statutory override for pooled fund valuation changes extended to 31 st March 2029
findings.detail: Gains and losses on investments held before 1st April 2024 go to an unusable reserve. They will only hit revenue when the holdings are sold or from 2029/30 if the override ends. The Council says its Capital Financing Reserve could cover any revenue impact.
findings.matters: Other councils with pooled fund losses will want to know the override now runs until 2029 and that the Council has a reserve in place to cover the risk.
findings.figures: Override until 31 st March 2029; Capital Financing Reserve (no amount given)
findings.quote: until 31 st March 2029

findings.paper_title: Treasury Management Performance Report 2026-27 - Quarter 2
findings.headline: Strategic pooled funds are valued at £7.807m at 30 September 2026 against £10.000m historic cost, up £0.103m in the year
findings.detail: The paper says the value has risen slightly from £7.704m at 31st March 2026 despite a weaker market for equities, bonds and property. The three funds are a £5.000m CCLA property fund and £5.000m in two ESG-focused funds.
findings.matters: A finance director at another council holding pooled funds will want to see how far fair value sits below cost and how the statutory override is protecting revenue.
findings.figures: £7.807m fair value at 30/09/2026; £10.000m historic cost; £7.704m at 31/03/2026; £0.103m increase
findings.quote: there has been a small increase of £0.103m in the value of the Council’s strategic investments to £7.807m

findings.paper_title: Treasury Management Performance Report 2026-27 - Quarter 2
findings.headline: Operational investments returned 3.78% for April to September 2026, against a 3.71% SONIA benchmark
findings.detail: Strategic investments are estimated at 4.25% for the same period, which the paper says is above the budgeted return. The paper gives the strategic budget as 4.04% in the main text and 4.02% in Appendix 3.
findings.matters: Investment income is offsetting part of the borrowing cost, which is why the financing budget is forecast under spend.
findings.figures: Operational: 3.78% against SONIA benchmark 3.71% (0.07% above); strategic: estimated 4.25% against budgeted 4.04% (0.21% above) in the main text, 4.02% in Appendix 3; average balance £49.534m
findings.quote: is 3.78%, which is 0.07% above the 7-Day Sterling Overnight Index Average (SONIA) benchmark rate of 3.71%

findings.paper_title: Treasury Management Performance Report 2026-27 - Quarter 2
findings.headline: Council took out £35.000m of new borrowing in April to September 2026, including £10.000m of delayed borrowing from 2025/26
findings.detail: The £35.000m breaks down as £10.000m of delayed 2025/26 borrowing, kept back to maintain the liquidity indicator above £15.000m, and £25.000m to replace maturing loans. Borrowing ended the quarter at £294.482m, down from £288.977m at 1st April 2026.
findings.matters: Replacing maturing loans and deferring borrowing to protect liquidity are both funding decisions other councils face in the same conditions.
findings.figures: £35.000m new loans; £10.000m delayed; £25.000m replacing maturing loans; £25.000m maturity repayments; £4.495m PWLB annuity principal repaid; £294.482m total at 30 September 2026
findings.quote: This includes £35.000m of borrowing taken out during the year

findings.paper_title: Treasury Management Performance Report 2026-27 - Quarter 2
findings.headline: The 20-year PWLB annuity rate rose from 5.54% at the end of February 2026 to 6.51% on 30th September
findings.detail: The paper links the rise to gilt yields, saying PWLB rates are priced 0.80% to 1.00% above gilts. The Council cites this as the reason for shortening the debt portfolio and for delaying borrowing.
findings.matters: PWLB is the usual source of replacement funding when a LOBO is repaid, so the current rate sets the cost of replacing any LOBO that has been repaid.
findings.figures: 5.54% at end February 2026; 6.51% at 30th September 2026; PWLB priced 0.80% to 1.00% above gilts
findings.quote: The 20-year PWLB annuity rate has risen from 5.54% at the end of February 2026 to 6.51% on 30th September.

findings.paper_title: Treasury Management Performance Report 2026-27 - Quarter 2
findings.headline: Council proposes raising the under-12-month and 12-to-24-month maturity limits on borrowing from 30% to 50% each
findings.detail: Officers have been shortening the duration of the debt portfolio to manage borrowing costs, and the paper asks Council to approve higher upper limits for debt maturing within two years. The other maturity bands are unchanged. The paper says the change has been discussed with Arlingclose, which supports it.
findings.matters: Raising short-dated limits lets a council take more refinancing risk in the near term; other councils and lenders will want to see whether this is a wider move away from long-dated borrowing.
findings.figures: Under 12 months: 30% to 50% (+20%); 12 months to 24 months: 30% to 50% (+20%); actual under 12 months at 30/09/2026: 25.47%
findings.quote: have been reducing the duration of its debt portfolio

findings.paper_title: Treasury Management Performance Report 2026-27 - Quarter 2
findings.headline: Interest and capital financing budget for 2026/27 is forecast at £1.450m under budget
findings.detail: The forecast underspend is attributed to delayed borrowing following the reprofiling of the capital programme and to higher investment returns. Debt costs are forecast £0.750m favourable and interest on balances £0.700m favourable.
findings.matters: A finance officer at another council can compare how much of a financing underspend comes from delayed borrowing against how much comes from higher cash returns.
findings.figures: £1.450m under budget; debt costs (£0.750m) FAV; interest on balances (£0.700m) FAV; total budgeted spend £5.311m, forecast £3.861m
findings.quote: is currently forecast to be £1.450m under budget

findings.paper_title: Treasury Management Performance Report 2026-27 - Quarter 2
findings.headline: KBC Bank N.V. LOBO loans totalling £10.000m are still listed as outstanding at a 4.50% variable rate after reaching the end of their fixed periods
findings.detail: Two KBC Bank N.V. loans of £5.000m each, both starting 08/10/2004 and ending 08/10/2054, appear in the 30 September 2026 borrowing portfolio at 4.50%. The footnote says the lender may change the rate at six-monthly intervals and that the borrower may then repay without penalty, but the paper does not say whether any rate change has been proposed or exercised.
findings.matters: A council still holding LOBOs after their reset is unusual, and a finance director or lender needs to know whether the lender has used its option and what the council has decided in response.
findings.quote: All LOBO’s have reached the end of their fixed interest period and have reverted to the variable rate of 4.50%.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 3 - Avon Pension Fund Committee Annual Report to Council (as at March 2026)
findings.headline: Avon Pension Fund received £259m in pension contributions and paid out £261m in pension payments and other benefits in 2025-26.
findings.detail: The paper gives the contribution and payment totals as a brief reference in the introduction. It does not comment on the net position between them, and the full figures are in the Fund's annual report.
findings.matters: A finance director at a participating council can compare the Fund's contribution and payment flows with the cash flows that matter for their own pension cost planning.
findings.figures: Contributions received £259m; payments and other benefits paid £261m; Fund value £5.8 billion at 31 March 2026
findings.quote: In 2025-26 the Fund received £259m in pension contributions and paid out £261m in pension payments and other benefits.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 3 - Avon Pension Fund Committee Annual Report to Council (as at March 2026)
findings.headline: Avon Pension Fund extended completion of its McCloud remedy exercise to August 2026.
findings.detail: The Fund used its discretion to extend the deadline, so the work can be completed accurately while other major regulatory projects proceed. The paper gives no earlier deadline for comparison.
findings.matters: Every LGPS fund has to complete McCloud remedy work, so a finance officer at another council can check their own timetable against this extension.
findings.figures: Completion extended to August 2026
findings.quote: exercised its discretion to extend completion of the remedy exercise to August 2026

findings.paper_title: Appendix 3 - Avon Pension Fund Committee Annual Report to Council (as at March 2026)
findings.headline: Internal Audit gave Level 3, Reasonable Assurance on Pension Payroll Processes and on Transfers Out during 2025-26.
findings.detail: Internal Audit completed two audits in the year, and both received the same assurance level. The paper does not record any further findings or management actions against them.
findings.matters: Audit assurance on payroll and transfers is a control result that a finance director at another council can compare with the outcome of their own internal audit programme.
findings.figures: Two audits completed, each at Level 3, Reasonable Assurance
findings.quote: Level 3, Reasonable Assurance

findings.paper_title: Appendix 3 - Avon Pension Fund Committee Annual Report to Council (as at March 2026)
findings.headline: Avon Pension Fund reports monthly administration performance consistently above 90% against key service measures by early 2026.
findings.detail: The paper links the improvement to successful recruitment, higher staff retention, investment in systems and process improvements. It says historic work backlogs were substantially reduced over the year.
findings.matters: A pension administration team recovering from backlogs is a common pressure at LGPS funds, and the Avon figures show one fund's route to meeting service standards.
findings.figures: Monthly performance consistently exceeding 90% against key service measures by early 2026
findings.quote: By early 2026, monthly performance levels were consistently exceeding 90% against key service measures.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 3 - Avon Pension Fund Committee Annual Report to Council (as at March 2026)
findings.headline: Avon Pension Fund increased its strategic allocation to Local Impact investments from 3% to 5% of Fund assets, or approximately £300m, by March 2026.
findings.detail: The Fund built its Local Impact portfolio across renewable infrastructure, affordable housing and small and medium-sized enterprise financing. The paper also records a new Natural Capital allocation approved in the same review.
findings.matters: A change in the allocation of a £5.8 billion fund toward local investment is a decision that other councils' pension committees may compare with their own strategies.
findings.figures: Allocation increased from 3% to 5% of Fund assets; approximately £300m; Fund value £5.8 billion
findings.quote: increase the strategic allocation to Local Impact investments from 3% to 5% of Fund assets or approximately £300m

findings.paper_title: Appendix 3 - Avon Pension Fund Committee Annual Report to Council (as at March 2026)
findings.headline: Avon Pension Fund agreed to replace Brunel Pension Partnership with Local Pensions Partnership Investments (LPPI) as its investment pool, with the change effective from 1 April 2026.
findings.detail: Brunel manages over 90% of the Fund's assets. The Committee reached its decision after a detailed options appraisal, and the Fund now expects to prepare a revised Investment Strategy Statement by March 2027.
findings.matters: Pool changes under the government's Fit for the Future reforms affect every LGPS fund, and the Avon transition shows how a fund in a pool gets from one operator to another.
findings.figures: Brunel manages over 90% of the assets in the Avon Pension Fund; Fund value £5.8 billion at 31 March 2026; revised Investment Strategy Statement due by March 2027
findings.quote: agreed to partner with LPPI

findings.paper_title: Appendix 3 - Avon Pension Fund Committee Annual Report to Council (as at March 2026)
findings.headline: Brunel Pension Partnership required £1.6m of additional capital to fund its solvent closure in 2025-26.
findings.detail: The paper says the additional capital is reflected in the Fund's total costs being over budget. Brunel was the Fund's pool operator, and the Committee moved the Fund to LPPI as a result of the government's pooling reforms.
findings.matters: Pooling exit costs such as this one are a question every council in an LGPS pool will face as the government's Fit for the Future reforms take effect.
findings.figures: £1.6m additional capital required by Brunel
findings.quote: This was reflected the additional capital of £1.6m required by Brunel to fund its solvent closure.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 3 - Avon Pension Fund Committee Annual Report to Council (as at March 2026)
findings.headline: Avon Pension Fund's total costs for 2025-26 were £31,942k against a budget of £31,673k, a difference of £269k.
findings.detail: The paper attributes the overspend mainly to the Investments line, which was £22,233k against a budget of £21,749k. Administration was £6,070k against £6,381k, and Governance was £3,639k against £3,543k.
findings.matters: The table shows an overspend on the Investments line that a finance officer at another council can compare with their own pension cost monitoring.
findings.figures: Total budget £31,673k, actual £31,942k, difference £269k; Investments budget £21,749k, actual £22,233k, difference £484k; Administration budget £6,381k, actual £6,070k, difference £311k; Governance budget £3,543k, actual £3,639k, difference £96k
findings.quote: During the year to 31 March 2026, total Fund costs were marginally over budget.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 3 - Avon Pension Fund Committee Annual Report to Council (as at March 2026)
findings.headline: Average employer contributions into the Avon Pension Fund fall from c.20% of salaries in 2023-26 to c.16% in the 2026-29 period.
findings.detail: The Foreword links the funding position from the 2025 valuation to support for employers. The fall in average contributions applies to the employers in the Fund, which include the four unitary authorities.
findings.matters: Employer contribution rates are a direct cost to councils and academies in the Fund, so a finance director at a participating authority would be affected by a change of this size.
findings.figures: c.20% of salaries during 2023-26; c.16% in the 2026-29 period
findings.quote: average contributions into the Fund declined from c.20% of salaries during 2023-26 to c.16% in the 2026-29 period.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 3 - Avon Pension Fund Committee Annual Report to Council (as at March 2026)
findings.headline: Avon Pension Fund's 2025 triennial valuation records a funding level of 106% at 31 March 2025, estimated at approximately 109% at 31 March 2026.
findings.detail: The Committee completed the 2025 triennial actuarial valuation and approved a new Funding Strategy Statement covering the three years from 1 April 2026. Based on the 2025 valuation assumptions, the funding level was estimated to have improved further by 31 March 2026.
findings.matters: A finance director at another council can compare this funding position with their own fund's valuation outcome, which drives employer contribution rates.
findings.figures: 106% funding level at 31 March 2025; approximately 109% estimated at 31 March 2026; long-term returns assumed at CPI +2.25% to CPI +3.30% per annum
findings.quote: The valuation confirmed that the Fund remains in a strong financial position, with a funding level of 106% at 31 March 2025, meaning that Fund assets exceed liabilities.

findings.paper_title: Liberal Democrat Motion on Overnight Visitor Levy
findings.headline: The motion asks that any visitor levy income not reduce other government funding allocations, and that it be ringfenced and passed to the unitary authority where it is raised.
findings.detail: The Council reaffirms that income raised should not be to the detriment of other government funding allocations and calls on government and the West of England Combined Authority Mayor to ringfence future visitor levy income for the unitary authorities to allocate independently. These are stated positions in a motion, not decisions.
findings.matters: Whether levy income is ringfenced or offset against existing grant determines whether it adds to a council's resources, which is a key modelling question for finance officers and for lenders assessing revenue capacity.
findings.quote: any income raised should not be to the detriment of other government funding allocations

findings.paper_title: Liberal Democrat Motion on Overnight Visitor Levy
findings.headline: The motion records that the government expects overnight visitor levy powers to be available from 2028, following the Visitor Levy (England) Bill introduced on 4 November 2026.
findings.detail: The motion welcomes the introduction of the Visitor Levy (England) Bill and cites a Budget Statement confirming the powers are expected from 2028. It also notes that the West of England Combined Authority Mayor supports an overnight visitor levy, subject to consultation.
findings.matters: A new discretionary local tax power with a stated start date of 2028 is a potential future revenue stream that finance directors would need to consider in medium-term budget planning, here and at other councils.
findings.figures: from 2028; 4 November 2026
findings.quote: that the powers are expected to be available from 2028

findings.paper_title: Appendix 4 - Local Pension Board Annual Report 2026
findings.headline: Local Pension Board 2025/26 spend of £12,709 against a £23,826 budget.
findings.detail: The Board's budget covers member allowances, training, recruitment and meeting costs. Recruitment spend was nil against a £5,000 budget, and training spend was £1,293 against £6,240, with a training subscription paid in July 2026 covering June 2026 to May 2027.
findings.matters: Under-spend on the statutory oversight body is small in cash terms, but it shows how a pension board's budget was used against plan, which a finance officer at another council may compare with their own pension governance costs.
findings.figures: £23,826 budget; £12,709 actual; £5,000 recruitment budget against £0 spent; £6,240 training budget

findings.paper_title: Appendix 4 - Local Pension Board Annual Report 2026
findings.headline: Avon Pension Fund's investment assets transferred from Brunel Pension Partnership to Local Pensions Partnership Investments (LPPI) on 1 April 2026.
findings.detail: The Board received regular updates on the transition programme, governance arrangements and associated risks before the transfer. The report records the Board as pleased to note the successful transfer of assets on that date, and the June 2026 meeting reviewed the successful transition.
findings.matters: Pooling transitions between LGPS pools are a live reform issue for every English pension fund, and a finance director at another council can see a completed transfer date and the governance steps that preceded it.
findings.figures: 1 April 2026
findings.quote: was pleased to note the successful transfer of assets to LPPI on 1 April 2026

findings.paper_title: Avon Pension Fund Annual Report to Council
findings.headline: Avon Pension Fund's Investment Panel is being replaced by an Investment Working Group that is an advisory group rather than a formal Local Government Committee.
findings.detail: The paper lists this as one of the Committee's terms of reference changes. The Investment Working Group will advise and will not be a formal committee of the Council.
findings.matters: A change from a formal committee to an advisory group alters where investment decisions are taken, which other funds may compare against their own structures.
findings.quote: Investment Panel replaced with Investment Working Group (IWG) which will be an advisory group not a formal Local Government Committee

findings.paper_title: Avon Pension Fund Annual Report to Council
findings.headline: Avon Pension Fund's Committee is removing the right of members to send substitutes, after a discussion in which the Committee reached a clear consensus.
findings.detail: The paper says the change was discussed in detail, with a clear consensus in favour of not allowing substitution because of the requirement for training and expertise. The Pension Board's quorum is also changing to any 3 members.
findings.matters: Other funds working through the same training and expertise requirements may face the same choice about whether substitution remains allowed.
findings.figures: any 3 members
findings.quote: Removal of right to substitute members of the Committee

findings.paper_title: Avon Pension Fund Annual Report to Council
findings.headline: Avon Pension Fund's investment pooling arrangements with Local Pension Partnership Investments (LPPI) are being added to the Committee's terms of reference.
findings.detail: The Committee's terms of reference are updated to include the new pooling arrangements, and the governance arrangements for the Investment Working Group and LPPI are placed in the Governance Strategy. The paper does not give pooling values or performance figures.
findings.matters: Pooling changes who makes and reports investment decisions, which affects how other funds in pools assess their own oversight arrangements.
findings.quote: New pooling arrangements with Local Pension Partnership Investments (LPPI)

findings.paper_title: Avon Pension Fund Annual Report to Council
findings.headline: Avon Pension Fund must confirm its statutory LGPS Senior Officer role before 31 December 2026, with the Head of Pensions proposed to take it on.
findings.detail: The paper says the Fund's current Head of Pensions role meets the formal criteria and that the Fund plans to adapt it as the LGPS Senior Officer, with the Director of Assurance, Risk & Pensions named as substitute. The role is a statutory requirement under the Fit for the Future regulations, which took effect on 1 April 2026.
findings.matters: Every administering authority in the LGPS must make the same appointment under the same deadline, so other finance and pensions officers can compare how the role is being assigned.
findings.figures: 31 December 2026
findings.quote: This is a statutory role which must be confirmed before 31 December 2026.

findings.paper_title: E3717_APPENDIX 4(i) Capital Virements Jul - Sep 2026-27
findings.headline: Capital virements for July to September 2026-27 total £20,935,656, with £11,409,681 in future years.
findings.detail: The paper's totals balance income and expenditure across the current-year virements and the future-years virements. Most of the future-years total comes from the Neighbourhood Services vehicle replacement line.
findings.matters: The scale of quarterly virements shows how much of the capital programme is being reshaped in-year, which a finance director would compare with their own quarterly movement.
findings.figures: £20,935,656 (current-year total, income and expenditure); £11,409,681 (future-years total)

findings.paper_title: E3717_APPENDIX 4(i) Capital Virements Jul - Sep 2026-27
findings.headline: Fashion Museum public realm works recognised at £1,256,000 in 2026-27 and £489,000 in future years, fully grant-funded.
findings.detail: An officer delegated decision of 10th July 2026 recognises WECA grant for initial public realm works at the Fashion Museum. The paper states the initial works are funded 100% by grant, with a further £489,000 in future years.
findings.matters: Fully grant-funded works carry no council capital cost on their current phase, which a finance director would compare against the council's own share on similar schemes.
findings.figures: £1,256,000 (CAP2627#041, WECA grant, 2026-27); £489,000 (FY CAP2627#005, WECA grant, future years)
findings.quote: for initial works funded 100% by grant.

findings.paper_title: E3717_APPENDIX 4(i) Capital Virements Jul - Sep 2026-27
findings.headline: Three capital decisions taken under urgent decision rule 3.5.15, including the £1,270,000 Somer Valley Links revenue allocation.
findings.detail: The paper records Single Member Decision E3710 for the new Somer Valley Links allocation as an urgent decision under Rule 3.5.15, and Single Member Decision E3724 for the Manvers Street contract sum as a special urgent decision under the same rule. These urgent-route decisions bypass the usual pre-decision timetable.
findings.matters: A finance director would want to know how often capital allocations are taken under urgent procedures, since that affects how they monitor cabinet approvals.
findings.figures: £1,270,000 (CAP2627#018, Somer Valley Links revenue); £920,000 (CAP2627#019, Manvers Street Remediation)
findings.quote: Urgent Decision Under Rule 3.5.15

findings.paper_title: E3717_APPENDIX 4(i) Capital Virements Jul - Sep 2026-27
findings.headline: £920,000 of capital contingency used for the Manvers Street Remediation contract sum, then reinstated in the same quarter.
findings.detail: On 4th June 2026 a Single Member Decision agreed the Manvers Street Remediation contract sum, funded by £920,000 moved out of capital contingency. CAP2627#060 restores the same £920,000 to contingency as a technical adjustment by the Director of Finance.
findings.matters: Contingency being drawn and then restored shows how a council is holding headroom for unplanned capital costs, which a finance director at another council would compare against their own contingency policy.
findings.quote: reinstate capital contingency funding temporarily

findings.paper_title: E3717_APPENDIX 4(i) Capital Virements Jul - Sep 2026-27
findings.headline: Somer Valley Links grant funding moved to Full Business Case approval, with £495,000 and £1,968,000 recognised in the period.
findings.detail: Two officer delegated decisions of 24th July and 14th August 2026 approved Full Business Case grant funding for Somer Valley Links. The paper recognises £495,000 under CAP2627#056 and £1,968,000 under CAP2627#058, with a £32,000 reduction in Midsomer Norton & Westfield WECA grant under CAP2627#059.
findings.matters: Moving a scheme to Full Business Case approval is a milestone that a finance director would track against the grant conditions and the scheme's funding profile.
findings.quote: approve Full Business Case grant funding for Somer Valley Links.

findings.paper_title: E3717_APPENDIX 4(i) Capital Virements Jul - Sep 2026-27
findings.headline: Neighbourhood Services vehicle replacement procurement approved over two years, with £10,530,000 added to future years.
findings.detail: A Director of Place officer decision of 21st July 2026 fully approved procurement of replacement vehicles over the next two years. The 2026-27 line adds £1,281,447 from SSB, and the future-years line adds £10,530,000 from SCB and SSB.
findings.matters: A finance director, here or elsewhere, would want to see how a multi-year vehicle fleet commitment is funded and how much of it falls outside the current year.
findings.figures: £1,281,447 (2026-27, SSB); £10,530,000 (future years, SCB,SSB); £10,530,000 future years total as written in the paper
findings.quote: to fully approve procurement of replacement vehicles over next two years

findings.paper_title: E3717_APPENDIX 4(ii) Capital Cashlimits Jul - Sep 2026-27
findings.headline: The Local Authority Housing Fund (Ukrainian/Afghan homes) budget rises £1.191m to £1.484m
findings.detail: The Local Authority Housing Fund scheme for Ukrainian and Afghan homes moves from £293k to £1.484m after a £1.191m virement, the largest single increase in the Built Environment, Housing and Sustainable Development portfolio. The paper does not give the reason.
findings.matters: A council that brings a government-backed housing fund scheme into its capital programme in the same period as its main funding changes is one a peer or lender would want to track.
findings.figures: Scheme budget £293k to £1,484k (virement £1,191k); portfolio total £13,908k to £15,100k (virement £1,191k)

findings.detail: The Resources portfolio gains £2.995m across its schemes. Neighbourhood Services Vehicles rises from £6.048m to £7.329m, and Commercial Estate Planned Maintenance Programme moves from -£311k to £1.043m after a £1.354m virement, while Commercial Estate Refurbishment Programme is reduced by £854k.
findings.matters: Vehicle replacement and commercial estate spend are both capital calls a council may need to fund from borrowing, and a finance director at another council would want to see the scale of these changes.

findings.quote: Neighbourhood Services Vehicles Cap1718036 6,048 1,281 7,329

findings.paper_title: E3717_APPENDIX 4(ii) Capital Cashlimits Jul - Sep 2026-27
findings.headline: The Sustainable Transport Delivery budget rises £15.107m to £50.311m, with CRSTS Somer Valley Links up £8.848m to £8.711m
findings.detail: The Sustainable Transport Delivery portfolio is the largest single movement in the table. Within it, CRSTS Somer Valley Links moves from a budget of -£136k to £8.711m, and CRSTS Bath Sustainable Walking & Cycling Links moves from -£98k to £3.976m after a £4.074m virement.
