findings.detail: The paper lists carry forwards from 2025/26 underspends across Corporate Office (£23,900), Inclusion & Prevention (£45,505) and Integrated Commissioning - CYP (£33,334). The paper says these were approved in the July 2026 Cabinet outturn report and the virement is one-off.
findings.matters: It shows how the 2025/26 outturn underspend is being returned to services in 2026/27, which is relevant to peers managing year-end carry-forward policy.
findings.figures: £102,739 total (£23,900 Corporate Office; £45,505 Inclusion & Prevention; £33,334 Integrated Commissioning - CYP)
findings.quote: Carry forwards from 2025/26 underspends, as approved by

findings.paper_title: E3717_APPENDIX 3(i) - Revenue Virements Nov'26
findings.headline: A £848,000 income target for Bath Quays South moves from Regeneration to the Commercial Estate.
findings.detail: Budget responsibility for the Bath Quays South income target is transferred from the Economic & Cultural Sustainable Development portfolio's Regeneration budget to the Commercial Estate team. The paper records approval by the relevant Cabinet Members in July 2026 and says the virement is ongoing.
findings.matters: A large income target is changing hands between teams, which matters to finance directors tracking whether commercial property income is being managed with clear ownership.
findings.figures: £848,000 (income target transferred to Commercial Estate, ongoing)
findings.quote: the responsibility of Bath Quays South.

findings.paper_title: E3717_APPENDIX 3(i) - Revenue Virements Nov'26
findings.headline: £120,000 of lost rental income from the redevelopment of a Commercial Estate asset is covered by a one-off allocation from revenue budget contingency.
findings.detail: The Commercial Estate income budget receives £120,000 from the corporate contingency. The paper states the allocation is one-off and relates to the redevelopment of a Commercial Estate asset.
findings.matters: It shows a rental income shortfall from a redevelopment being met from contingency rather than a service budget, with a one-off rather than recurring funding source.
findings.figures: £120,000 (from Corporate Budgets, one-off)
findings.quote: to cover lost rental income due to redevelopment of Commercial Estate asset.

findings.paper_title: E3717_APPENDIX 3(i) - Revenue Virements Nov'26
findings.headline: A corporately held budget of £4,016,306 is distributed to services for the 2026/27 pay award following national agreement.
findings.detail: The pay award budget is moved out of the Corporate Budgets line into service cashlimits as an ongoing virement. The paper describes it as a distribution of the corporately held budget for the 2026/27 pay award.
findings.matters: A finance director at another council can compare how a national pay settlement is being funded in year, here from a central corporate budget rather than service cashlimits.
findings.figures: £4,016,306 (transfer from Corporate Budgets incl. Capital, Audit & Bank Charges, ongoing)
findings.quote: Distribution of corporately held budget for 2026/27 Pay Award following national agreement.

findings.paper_title: E3717_APPENDIX 5 - Revenue Savings Monitor
findings.headline: Home to School Transport cost reduction of £150k is shown with no 2026/27 delivery, with the council reporting a forecast overspend
findings.detail: The paper reports that delivery was delayed by key officer sickness and that the management post has now been filled. The council says it will review routes and contract costs to mitigate the forecast overspend, with a revised forecast to be given in the quarter 3 monitor.
findings.matters: Home to school transport is a demand-led cost pressure in many councils, and a forecast overspend that is still being worked on at mid-year is worth tracking.
findings.figures: £150k saving value, delayed until 2027/28; £150k on-going budget pressure
findings.quote: Delivery has been delayed through key officer sickness, but is expected to get back on track now the management post has been filled.

findings.paper_title: E3717_APPENDIX 5 - Revenue Savings Monitor
findings.headline: Transforming Customer Services saving of £300k will not be realised until 2027/28 because the service redesign timetable has been delayed
findings.detail: The saving is linked to a new customer services technology platform that is intended to reduce back-office spend. The council reports that the delay means the benefits fall into 2027/28.
findings.matters: A technology-enabled back-office saving that slips a year is a common pattern that peers planning similar digital programmes will compare against.
findings.figures: £300k saving value, delayed until 2027/28
findings.quote: Delayed service redesign timetable has meant benefits will not be realised until 2027/28

findings.paper_title: E3717_APPENDIX 5 - Revenue Savings Monitor
findings.headline: Adult Services savings of £2,735k and Children's Services savings of £465k are reported as fully delivered
findings.detail: The Adult Services portfolio total shows £2,705k permanent and £30k one-off delivery against £2,735k of savings. The Children's Services total shows the full £465k delivered, with the reunifications and off-contract spend savings achieved from actions in residential placements.
findings.matters: Two of the largest social care savings lines being reported as fully delivered shows a different picture from the undelivered lines elsewhere in the same paper.
findings.figures: Adult Services £2,735k delivered (£2,705k permanent, £30k one-off); Children's Services £465k delivered

findings.paper_title: E3717_APPENDIX 5 - Revenue Savings Monitor
findings.headline: A £350k Business Change resource saving is reported as delivered through the flexible use of capital receipts in 2026/27
findings.detail: Staffing in the business change function is to prioritise transformation projects with financial benefits and is funded from available capital receipts. The saving is recorded as delivered for 2026/27 on that basis.
findings.matters: Using capital receipts to fund revenue transformation staff is a flexible-use decision that finance directors and lenders watch when judging the sustainability of the revenue position.
findings.figures: £350k permanent saving value and delivery
findings.quote: Saving delivered, flexible use of capital receipts to fund transformation resource in 2026/27

findings.paper_title: E3717_APPENDIX 5 - Revenue Savings Monitor
findings.headline: Bath Quays South lettings savings of £100k in 2026/27 and £150k in 2025/26 are reported as not achievable with current tenants
findings.detail: The council says the income target has been increased over several years and that the latest increase cannot be met with the tenants in place. It also reports no new tenants in the pipeline, so the saving is shown as an on-going budget pressure.
findings.matters: An office income target that has been stretched over several years and has no pipeline is a concrete example of commercial income assumptions failing to hold.
findings.figures: £100k 2026/27 saving, shown as on-going budget pressure; £150k 2025/26 undelivered saving, delayed until 2027/28
findings.quote: no new tenants in the pipeline.

findings.paper_title: E3717_APPENDIX 5 - Revenue Savings Monitor
findings.headline: Sustainable Transport Strategy savings of £1,280k show £660k delivered, with the parking income saving for moving traffic enforcement moved to 2027/28
findings.detail: The portfolio total shows £660k delivered against a £1,280k target, with £620k variance. The Moving Traffic Enforcement saving is delayed because of a later go-live and a warning-letter period, and is forecast as deliverable in full for 2027/28. The commentary also reports pressures across most parking income streams.
findings.matters: Parking income is a common source of savings in councils, and a finance director elsewhere will want to know how a late enforcement start has affected the income line.
findings.figures: £1,280k portfolio savings target; £660k delivered; £620k variance; £320k delayed until 2027/28; £300k on-going budget pressure; Moving Traffic Enforcement £250k target, £100k delivered
findings.quote: but are forecast as deliverable in full for 2027/28.

findings.paper_title: E3717_APPENDIX 5 - Revenue Savings Monitor
findings.headline: The Being Our Best Programme staffing saving of £2,000k shows £1,075k delivered, with a £743k shortfall reported as contributing to the bottom line forecast adverse variance
findings.detail: The paper attributes the shortfall to delays in restructuring. Part of it has been covered by vacancy management, but the remaining £743k is recorded as part of the council's forecast adverse variance.
findings.matters: A large staffing saving that is part-delivered and feeds the bottom-line variance is a specific test for any council running a similar restructuring programme.
findings.figures: £2,000k permanent saving value; £1,075k permanent savings delivery; £925k variance; £743k shortfall
findings.quote: the £743k shortfall is contributing to the council's bottom line forecast adverse variance

findings.paper_title: E3717_APPENDIX 5 - Revenue Savings Monitor
findings.headline: Undelivered 2025/26 savings of £2,715k show £1,325k delivered, with £1,058k delayed until 2027/28 and £150k of on-going budget pressure
findings.detail: Savings carried forward from 2025/26 are reported separately from the 2026/27 proposals. The table records how much of the carried-forward target has been delivered, how much is delayed, and how much remains as on-going pressure.
findings.matters: Carry-forward savings that slip again are a signal to lenders and peers of how far recurring savings targets are depending on later years.
findings.figures: £2,715k undelivered 2025/26 savings target; £1,325k delivered; £1,390k variance; £1,058k delayed until 2027/28; £182k mitigated by one-off underspend or income; £150k on-going budget pressure

findings.paper_title: E3717_APPENDIX 5 - Revenue Savings Monitor
findings.headline: 2026/27 savings show £6,393k delivered against a £1,245k variance, with £770k delayed until 2027/28 and £405k of on-going budget pressure
findings.detail: The council total for 2026/27 shows permanent and one-off savings delivery against the saving values in the table. The variance is split between savings delayed until 2027/28, savings mitigated by one-off underspends or income, and on-going budget pressure.
findings.matters: A finance director at another council can compare how much of a savings programme has slipped into the next year and how much has become a permanent budget pressure.
findings.figures: £6,393k total savings delivery; £1,245k total savings variance; £770k delayed until 2027/28; £70k mitigated by one-off underspend or income; £405k on-going budget pressure

findings.paper_title: E3717 Revenue and Capital Budget Monitoring - 202627 Quarter 2
findings.headline: Improving Communications and Letterbox to Inbox savings of £0.522m are delayed to 2027/28.
findings.detail: The paper says the savings are held within Customer Services at present and are expected to be delivered in full in 2027/28.
findings.matters: A savings delay of this kind is one a finance director at another council may recognise in its own transformation programme, and the paper gives the deferral date.
findings.figures: £0.522m delayed savings; 2027/28 expected delivery date
findings.quote: have been delayed but are expected to be delivered in full in 2027/28, which are held in Customer Services at present (£0.522m).

findings.paper_title: E3717 Revenue and Capital Budget Monitoring - 202627 Quarter 2
findings.headline: The council tax collection fund forecast is an in-year surplus of £0.269m, of which the council's share is £0.223m.
findings.detail: The paper attributes the favourable trend mainly to Local Council Tax Support costs being under budget and to long-term empty property premiums. This is offset by more exempt properties and reclassifications.
findings.matters: Council tax surplus or deficit positions feed the following year's budget, so a surplus is a source of future funding for other councils to compare.
findings.figures: £0.269m in-year surplus; £0.223m council share; 0.2% positive variance; Local Council Tax Support £10.667m against £11.064m budget
findings.quote: The current forecast on Council Tax is an in-year collection fund surplus of £0.269m.

findings.paper_title: E3717 Revenue and Capital Budget Monitoring - 202627 Quarter 2
findings.headline: The business rates collection fund is projected to be a £0.631m deficit for the council's share, including the 2025/26 carry-forward.
findings.detail: The in-year business rates deficit is £0.837m, of which the council's share is £0.787m. The paper also reports a £1.125m adverse provision for appeals, mainly for the 2023 rating list, and a £0.288m favourable forecast in gross rates after reliefs.
findings.matters: Business rates volatility is a shared pressure across councils after the 2026 revaluation and the 2026/27 system reset, and the paper gives the appeals provision as a separate figure.
findings.figures: £0.631m projected council-share deficit; £0.837m in-year deficit; £0.787m council share of in-year deficit; £1.125m appeals provision; £0.288m favourable gross rates; £1.077m safety net payment
findings.quote: for a projected deficit of £0.631m.

findings.paper_title: E3717 Revenue and Capital Budget Monitoring - 202627 Quarter 2
findings.headline: The General Fund un-earmarked reserve has a current uncommitted balance of £12.584m, within the £12.000m to £13.200m range set by the risk assessment.
findings.detail: The paper says the reserve is held corporately to manage in-year financial pressures that cannot be mitigated within existing budget and financial planning reserve levels.
findings.matters: A finance director can see the headroom above the minimum of the risk range, and compare it with their own un-earmarked reserve position.
findings.figures: £12.584m uncommitted balance; £12.000m to £13.200m risk range
findings.quote: The risk assessment has set a range of between £12.000m and £13.200m to meet those risks in the 2026/27 financial year.

findings.paper_title: E3717 Revenue and Capital Budget Monitoring - 202627 Quarter 2
findings.headline: Forecast unapplied capital receipts are £3.097m against £3.572m budgeted, including the expected sale of Lewis House before year end.
findings.detail: The paper says £1.675m has been received in 2026/27 so far, and that £2.700m was carried forward from 2025/26.
findings.matters: Capital receipts from disposals are the funding source for flexible use of capital receipts and for reducing borrowing, so a shortfall against budget affects both the revenue budget and the borrowing position.
findings.figures: £3.097m forecast receipts; £3.572m budgeted; £1.675m received so far; £2.700m carried forward from 2025/26
findings.quote: further forecast of £3.097m against £3.572m budgeted, including the sale of Lewis House expected before year end.

findings.paper_title: E3717 Revenue and Capital Budget Monitoring - 202627 Quarter 2
findings.headline: Property Company Investment is £13.911m lower than budget, due to lower Aequus loan drawdowns.
findings.detail: The paper attributes the lower drawdowns to delays in the development pipeline. It is the largest single scheme variance within the Resources portfolio.
findings.matters: A council that is lending to a development company, or is exposed to its drawdown timing, will want to see how a delay of this size is treated in the capital and revenue position.
findings.figures: £13.911m in-year variance; Resources portfolio variance £18.616m; £17.289m rephased to future years
findings.quote: Property Company Investment £13.911m – lower Aequus loan drawn-downs due to development pipeline delays.

findings.paper_title: E3717 Revenue and Capital Budget Monitoring - 202627 Quarter 2
findings.headline: The 2026/27 capital programme is forecast at £122.579m against a budget of £158.077m, with £34.055m rephased into future years.
findings.detail: The Resources and Economic and Cultural Sustainable Development portfolios account for most of the variance. The paper gives the scheme-level reasons for the reprofiling.
findings.matters: A finance director can see how much of a capital budget is being carried forward, which feeds into future borrowing and revenue costs.
findings.figures: £122.579m forecast; £158.077m revised budget; £35.498m variance; £34.055m rephased to future years
findings.quote: The current position of the 2026/27 Capital Programme is a forecast of £122.579m against a budget of £158.077m.

findings.paper_title: E3717 Revenue and Capital Budget Monitoring - 202627 Quarter 2
findings.headline: The 2026/27 pay award was finalised at 3.3%, against 3.0% assumed in the budget, and the £0.200m cost is met from a reserve.
findings.detail: The paper says the additional cost has been funded from the Job Evaluation and Pay Structure Reserve, and that budgets have been allocated across all services.
findings.matters: A finance director at another council can compare the outturn pay award with the assumption in their own budget, and see the reserve used to fund the difference.
findings.figures: 3.3% pay award; 3.0% budgeted; £0.200m cost pressure; reserve balance £1.047m brought forward and £0.687m estimated at 31/03/2027
findings.quote: The 2026/27 pay award was finalised at 3.3%, higher than the 3.0% that was assumed in the budget.

findings.paper_title: E3717 Revenue and Capital Budget Monitoring - 202627 Quarter 2
findings.headline: Home to School Transport has a forecast pressure of £0.818m, with partial offset of £0.514m from income and vacancy management.
findings.detail: The paper says demand is rising across a higher number of schools, which has led to more routes and higher costs.
findings.matters: Home-to-school transport is a statutory demand service that several councils are reporting as under pressure, so a specific figure with a stated offset is comparable.
findings.figures: £0.818m forecast pressure; £0.514m offset from income and vacancy management in the Network and Traffic Management Service
findings.quote: Home to School Transport has a forecast pressure of £0.818m as demand levels continue to rise across a higher volume of schools.

findings.paper_title: E3717 Revenue and Capital Budget Monitoring - 202627 Quarter 2
findings.headline: Older people's residential placements stood at 152 at the end of August 2026, against 145 at August 2025.
findings.detail: The paper says 2025/26 ended with a rise of over 10% year on year in this area. Residential care and home care are the pressure areas in the older people's service.
findings.matters: Placement numbers are a leading indicator of future spend, and the paper gives the year-on-year change over a specific period.
findings.figures: 152 residential placements at August 2026; 145 at August 2025; rise of over 10% year on year in 2025/26
findings.quote: the number of residential placements stood at 152 as at the end of August 2026, compared to 145 at August 2025.

findings.paper_title: E3717 Revenue and Capital Budget Monitoring - 202627 Quarter 2
findings.headline: Adult Services forecasts a £1.585m favourable variance, which the paper describes as a one-off in-year benefit.
findings.detail: The paper says the favourable position comes from transformation activities, and that residential placement demand in the older people's service continues to rise.
findings.matters: A finance director can see that the favourable position is one-off, so it will not repeat into the next year's budget.
findings.figures: £1.585m favourable variance; £72.799m revised budget; £71.214m year-end forecast
findings.quote: This favourable variance is a one-off in-year benefit only and is not anticipated to on an ongoing basis in future years.

findings.paper_title: E3717 Revenue and Capital Budget Monitoring - 202627 Quarter 2
findings.headline: A High Needs Stability Grant of £41.938m is expected on 30 November 2026, after the council's SEND Reform Plan was accepted in October 2026.
findings.detail: The paper says the grant must be held until the statutory override ends on 31 March 2028, and then used to fund the DSG deficit.
findings.matters: A finance director can see that a single grant payment is being earmarked against the DSG deficit, and can compare the timing and conditions with their own SEND reform position.
findings.figures: £41.938m High Needs Stability Grant; expected 30 November 2026; statutory override ends 31 March 2028
findings.quote: with a High Needs Stability Grant payment to the Council of £41.938m High Needs Stability Grant expected on 30th November 2026.

findings.paper_title: E3717 Revenue and Capital Budget Monitoring - 202627 Quarter 2
findings.headline: The Dedicated Schools Grant deficit was £46.505m at the end of 2025/26, and a further £19.615m overspend is forecast for 2026/27.
findings.detail: The paper says the DSG variance is ringfenced and does not impact the General Fund. The overspend is attributed to costs of supporting pupils with special educational needs and disabilities.
findings.matters: A cumulative DSG deficit of this size is a balance-sheet and cash question for councils, and the paper shows the current-year addition as well as the cumulative figure.
findings.figures: £46.505m cumulative DSG deficit at end of 2025/26; £13.716m 2025/26 overspend; £19.615m forecast 2026/27 overspend
findings.quote: The Dedicated Schools Grant (DSG) overspent by £13.716m for 2025/26 taking the cumulative to deficit at the end of 2025/26 to £46.505m.

findings.paper_title: E3717 Revenue and Capital Budget Monitoring - 202627 Quarter 2
findings.headline: Bath Quays South is forecast £0.872m adverse from unlet office space, and the Housing Delivery Vehicle is £0.625m over budget.
findings.detail: The paper attributes the Housing Delivery Vehicle position to delays in development projects, which move the timing of profit generation and dividend payments. Both pressures are to be met from the Commercial Income Risk Reserve.
findings.matters: Commercial property and development-company income is a common source of council pressure, and this paper shows the exposure for one specific building and one company.
findings.figures: £0.872m Bath Quays South adverse variance; £0.625m Housing Delivery Vehicle over budget; £0.618m Commercial Estate budget shortfall
findings.quote: Additionally the Bath Quays South property has an adverse variance of £0.872m from the unlet office space in the building.

findings.paper_title: E3717 Revenue and Capital Budget Monitoring - 202627 Quarter 2
findings.headline: The Corporate Estate is forecast £1.243m over budget, and the paper states a credible route to balance in 2027/28.
findings.detail: The paper identifies unachievable income and high holding costs for void estate as the cause. It says the balance will come from rationalising and disposing of surplus estate.
findings.matters: A finance director can see a specific asset-disposal plan that is being used to clear a recurring income gap, and can compare the timing with their own estate programme.
findings.figures: £1.243m in-year pressure; variance at the Guildhall, Hollies, Lewis House and Culverhay
findings.quote: There is a credible route to a balanced position in 2027/28 as surplus estate is rationalised and/or disposed of.

findings.paper_title: E3717 Revenue and Capital Budget Monitoring - 202627 Quarter 2
findings.headline: Roman Baths visitor numbers are 5% down on budget, and the forecast income shortfall has been reduced from about £1.0m to a £0.541m variance.
findings.detail: The paper says the shortfall is driven mainly by fewer group visitors to Bath. Mitigations are cost savings, strong corporate hire performance and a price increase in the last quarter of the year.
findings.matters: Heritage and visitor income is a discretionary income line that several councils have set against reserves, and the paper shows a mitigated outcome for a specific site.
findings.figures: 5% below budgeted visitor numbers; 3% below prior year; approximately £1.0m forecast income reduction; £0.541m forecast variance after mitigation; £13.261m net surplus budget
findings.quote: The Roman Baths visitor numbers are 3% down on prior year and 5% down on budget.

findings.paper_title: E3717 Revenue and Capital Budget Monitoring - 202627 Quarter 2
findings.headline: Interest rates on both borrowing and cash balances are favourable to the budget set in February 2026, an estimated £1.450m benefit.
findings.detail: The paper attributes the favourable variance in Resources – Corporate to treasury management, and expects an additional £0.250m from City Deal business rates pooling.
findings.matters: Treasury gains are offsetting service pressures in this council, and a lender or finance director will want to know how much of the position depends on rates staying where they are.
findings.figures: £1.450m estimated treasury benefit; £0.250m City Deal business rates pooling; Resources – Corporate favourable variance £1.695m
findings.quote: Interest rates have been favourable when compared to what was expected at budget setting on both borrowing and cash balances, resulting in an estimated £1.450m benefit to the council.

findings.paper_title: E3717 Revenue and Capital Budget Monitoring - 202627 Quarter 2
findings.headline: £1.325m (49%) of £2.715m undelivered 2025/26 savings are forecast as achieved.
findings.detail: The paper says the balance of £1.390m is mitigated by one-off underspends, or is delayed or undeliverable.
findings.matters: Savings carried over from a previous year that are still not delivered weigh on the next year's budget, and other councils with similar carry-forward lists will want to see how it is being handled.
findings.figures: £1.325m (49%) forecast achieved; £2.715m undelivered 2025/26 savings; £1.390m balance
findings.quote: £1.325m (49%) of these are forecast as achieved, leaving a balance of £1.390m as mitigated by one-off underspends, delayed or undeliverable.

findings.paper_title: E3717 Revenue and Capital Budget Monitoring - 202627 Quarter 2
findings.headline: £6.393m (84%) of 2026/27 savings are forecast as delivered, against £7.638m of savings to be delivered.
findings.detail: The remainder is either being mitigated through alternative measures or flagged as delayed or undeliverable. The paper says the £7.638m total is after removing £0.395m of reversals of 2025/26 one-off savings.
findings.matters: Savings delivery percentages are a direct check on whether a council's medium-term plan is holding, and this paper gives the forecast delivery rate for the current year.
findings.figures: £6.393m (84%) forecast delivered; £7.638m total 2026/27 savings to be delivered; £7.243m approved net savings; £0.395m reversals
findings.quote: At present £6.393m (84%) savings are forecast as delivered

findings.paper_title: E3717 Revenue and Capital Budget Monitoring - 202627 Quarter 2
findings.headline: The full £2.680m corporate contingency is released, and the forecast assumes £2.657m is drawn from the Commercial Income Risk Reserve.
findings.detail: The reserve had a brought-forward balance of £3.942m. The paper states that the contingency is not sufficient to offset all financial pressures across the organisation.
findings.matters: A finance director can see how much of a commercial income reserve is being used in a single year against a rising list of income shortfalls.
findings.figures: £2.680m contingency fully released; £2.657m reserve drawdown; £3.942m reserve balance brought forward from 2025/26; £1.104m estimated balance at 31/03/2027
findings.quote: The Quarter 2 forecast assumes that £2.657m of this reserve will be required to mitigate against the overall forecast position.

findings.paper_title: E3717 Revenue and Capital Budget Monitoring - 202627 Quarter 2
findings.headline: Children’s Services forecasts being £7.391m over budget at Quarter 2, within the Quarter 1 risk range of £5.4m to £8.9m.
findings.detail: The paper says the service closed 2025/26 with a £10.182m overspend. The 2026/27 pressure is £7.073m in Children’s Social Care and £0.318m in Education. Residential placement pressures total £5.890m and a £1.351m salary pressure comes from agency use.
findings.matters: Children’s residential placement costs are a common pressure across English councils, and this paper gives the split between placements, agency staffing and step-across placements.
findings.figures: £7.391m Quarter 2 over budget; £7.073m Children’s Social Care; £0.318m Education; £10.182m 2025/26 overspend; £5.890m residential placements; £1.351m salary pressure; £5.4m to £8.9m Quarter 1 risk range
findings.quote: the Quarter 2 forecast position is over budget by £7.391m

findings.paper_title: E3717 Revenue and Capital Budget Monitoring - 202627 Quarter 2
findings.headline: The General Fund forecast at Quarter 2 is a £3.725m adverse variance, against £5.320m at Quarter 1.
findings.detail: The forecast is stated after the use of the £2.680m corporate contingency and a projected £2.657m drawdown from the Commercial Income Risk Reserve. The paper says the Quarter 1 forecast was prepared on a risk-based approach.
findings.matters: A finance director at another council can compare how the same in-year pressure has moved between Quarter 1 and Quarter 2, and what it took to reduce it.
findings.figures: £3.725m Quarter 2 adverse variance; £5.320m Quarter 1 adverse position; £2.680m contingency released; £2.657m Commercial Income Risk Reserve drawdown
findings.quote: The forecast General Fund revenue budget outturn position as at Quarter 2 is an adverse net variance of £3.725m.

findings.paper_title: E3743_APPPENDIX 1_Transformation Plan 2026-2031
findings.headline: The council has a time-limited transformation fund that it says will not be used for business-as-usual costs or general service pressures.
findings.detail: The paper describes the fund as targeted and time-limited investment in capacity, capability and enabling activity. It lists uses such as specialist expertise, digital and data improvements and workforce change. The paper does not state the size of the fund.
findings.matters: Finance directors reviewing how transformation is funded will note that the paper sets out the fund's purpose and limits but gives no amount.
findings.quote: The fund will not be used to support ongoing business-as-usual costs or general service pressures.

findings.paper_title: E3743_APPPENDIX 1_Transformation Plan 2026-2031
findings.headline: The paper says plans for each programme are still being developed and that the savings figures will be refined through 2026/27 ahead of the February 2027 budget.
findings.detail: The paper states that full programme details will be in the final budget papers and that delivery plans for the savings will be developed through the rest of 2026/27. It also says a delivery plan covering each workstream is to be in place from April 2027.
findings.matters: A finance officer watching how peers handle savings planning can see the timetable the council has set for converting the indicative figures into a budget and delivery plan.
findings.figures: February 2027 budget setting; April 2027 plan start
findings.quote: This will be in place for the start date of the plan in April 2027.

findings.paper_title: E3743_APPPENDIX 1_Transformation Plan 2026-2031
findings.headline: The plan lists £7.250m of assumed savings for 2027/28 across three themes, with Prevention contributing £4.000m and Productivity £2.000m.
findings.detail: The table covers 2027/28 only and gives Prevention £4.000m, Place Shaping £1.250m and Productivity £2.000m, which it describes as the 'current assumed level of savings'. Home to School Transport is £0.250m and the operational estate is £1.000m within Place Shaping. The paper says the impact on future years will be assessed later.
findings.matters: Set against the £28.0m three-year requirement in the same paper, the 2027/28 figure is the first year's identified amount, which a finance director can track in the February 2027 budget.
findings.figures: £7.250m total 2027/28; Prevention £4.000m; Productivity £2.000m; Place Shaping £1.250m; Home to School Transport £0.250m; operational estate £1.000m
findings.quote: The following table summarises the current assumed level of savings associated with each workstream.

findings.paper_title: E3743_APPPENDIX 1_Transformation Plan 2026-2031
findings.headline: The council says the Fair Funding Review is reducing its funding by nearly £13m over three years.
findings.detail: The paper names the government's Fair Funding Review as a reason that funding is not keeping pace with demand. It says prudent financial management and strong commercial income, which it describes as historically relied on, are no longer sufficient on their own.
findings.matters: Other councils and lenders can measure the scale of the funding reduction the council attributes to the Fair Funding Review against their own exposure to the same reform.
findings.figures: nearly £13m reduction in funding over three years
findings.quote: which is reducing our funding by nearly £13m over three years

findings.paper_title: E3743_APPPENDIX 1_Transformation Plan 2026-2031
findings.headline: Bath and North East Somerset Council says it must find £28.0m of savings over three years, equivalent to nearly 15% of its net revenue budget.
findings.detail: The paper states that the council must find £28.0m of savings over the next three years. It says many of the obvious solutions have already been implemented, and that this figure must be achieved against historically high inflation and rising demand.
findings.matters: A finance director at another council can compare the size of this three-year savings requirement, expressed as a share of net revenue budget, with their own, and the paper's note on exhausted options is a point of reference for peers.
findings.figures: £28.0m savings over three years; nearly 15% of net revenue budget
findings.quote: Over the next three years we must find £28.0m of savings, equivalent to nearly 15% of our net revenue budget.

findings.paper_title: E3744_Q2 2627 Corporate Strategy Performance Report
findings.headline: Care home admissions stood at 120.2 per 100,000 population against a target of 161.3, on a downward trend over recent quarters.
findings.detail: The paper links the lower admissions to more people remaining in community settings for longer. It reports this as an adult social care indicator on target.
findings.matters: Lower residential care admissions indicate a shift toward community care, which bears directly on the cost mix of adult social care provision.
findings.figures: 120.2 admissions per 100,000 population; target 161.3 per 100,000 population
findings.quote: Care Home admissions per 100k is 120.2 vs target 161.3, with a downward trend over recent quarters, supporting more people to remain in community settings for longer.

findings.paper_title: E3744_Q2 2627 Corporate Strategy Performance Report
findings.headline: Children looked after stood at 66.26 per 10,000 children, up 2%, and the paper says this is above the England average.
findings.detail: The paper attributes the rise mainly to unaccompanied asylum-seeking children and older adolescents entering care in crisis. It describes the trend as upward over recent quarters.
findings.matters: Looked-after placements are among the largest demand-led costs in children's services, so a rising rate above the national average is directly relevant to budget planning.
findings.figures: 66.26 children looked after per 10,000 children; +2% change
findings.quote: Children looked after per 10k are 66.26 (+2%), trending upward over recent quarters.

findings.paper_title: E3744_Q2 2627 Corporate Strategy Performance Report
findings.headline: Children on Education Health & Care Plans total 2,959, up 4%, with the paper expecting numbers to stay elevated until national SEND reforms take effect.
findings.detail: The paper describes the trend as clearly upward over recent years and says demand is high but in line with previous patterns. It expects elevated levels to continue until national SEND reforms and new DfE legislation take effect.
findings.matters: EHCP numbers are a central driver of high-needs education spending, and the paper states no timeline for when the national reforms will change the trajectory.
findings.figures: 2,959 children; +4% change
findings.quote: Children on Education Health & Care Plans (EHCP) total 2,959 (+4%), with a clear upward trend over recent years.

findings.paper_title: E3744_Q2 2627 Corporate Strategy Performance Report
findings.headline: Households in temporary accommodation stood at 82 against a target of 90, up 19% in the latest quarter.
findings.detail: The paper attributes the rise to families needing accommodation, with demand linked to landlord exits rather than reduced move-on supply. It records the figure as on target despite the quarterly increase.
findings.matters: Temporary accommodation placements are a homelessness cost that finance teams track closely, and a sharp quarterly rise in households is the kind of demand change that feeds into that spend.
findings.figures: 82 households; target 90 households; +19% change in the latest quarter
findings.quote: Households in temporary accommodation is 82 vs target 90,but has increased +19% in the latest quarter.

findings.paper_title: E3743_ Transformation Plan Nov 2026
findings.headline: The draft B&NES Transformation Plan 2027–2032 does not yet quantify costs, benefits or savings, which are to be developed for each workstream through the budget and Medium Term Financial Strategy process.
findings.detail: The paper states that the Plan is a strategic framework and does not itself authorise spending or service decisions. It says detailed costs, benefits and savings will be set out later through the budget and MTFS process. It also says the Transformation Fund is targeted, time-limited investment that will not support ongoing business-as-usual costs or general service pressures.
findings.matters: A finance director at this council or elsewhere can see that the transformation savings are not yet costed in this paper, so any benefit from the programme will depend on the later MTFS work.
findings.figures: None in this paper. No savings, costs, or Transformation Fund amount is stated.
findings.quote: Detailed delivery plans, costs, benefits and savings for each workstream will be developed and refined through the budget and Medium Term Financial Strategy process.

findings.paper_title: E3717_APPENDIX 1 - Revenue Monitor Commentary
findings.headline: Children's Services delivered £465k of 2026/27 budgeted savings in full, the paper states.
findings.detail: The paper reports that the budgeted savings for children's services were fully delivered, while separate staffing and placement pressures remain in the same cashlimit. A service redesign aligned to the government's Families First initiative is underway.
findings.matters: Delivering savings in full while the same budget is overspending shows a finance director the split between savings delivery and demand-led pressure, which matters for benchmarking.
findings.figures: Budgeted savings £465k for 2026/27; forecast overspend £7,008k
findings.quote: Budgeted savings of £465k for 26/27 have been fully delivered.

findings.paper_title: E3717_APPENDIX 1 - Revenue Monitor Commentary
findings.headline: Cloud hosting infrastructure costs have fallen from ~£45,000 to ~£40,000 per month from 1 September, with a predicted ~£37,000 by March 2027 saving £96,000 per year.
findings.detail: The paper attributes the IT overspend of £87k to systems migrating to cloud SaaS taking longer than predicted, including Unit4 Finance and Northgate Revs & Bens. It says monthly costs will continue to reduce over the coming months.
findings.matters: A specific monthly cloud cost reduction tied to a named finance system migration gives peers a benchmark for the savings from moving to SaaS hosting.
findings.figures: Monthly cloud infrastructure cost ~£45,000 reduced to ~£40,000; predicted ~£37,000 by March 2027; annual saving £96,000; IT forecast variance £87k adverse
findings.quote: Cloud monthly infrastructure costs have been reduced from ~£45,000 per month to ~£40,000 from 1st September.

findings.paper_title: E3717_APPENDIX 1 - Revenue Monitor Commentary
findings.headline: Corporate Estate forecast £1,243k adverse, with budgeted disposal and redeployment savings described as "stubborn to achieve".
findings.detail: The paper attributes the pressure to market conditions for disposal or redeployment, a delay in centralising budgets through the Corporate Landlord, and property costs on void assets. It identifies material forecast risk of around £1.000m and names estate rationalisation as the main mitigation.
findings.matters: Property rationalisation savings slipping is a recurring issue for councils with large estates, and the paper ties the delay to market conditions and the corporate landlord transition.
findings.figures: Corporate Estate variance £1,243k adverse; forecast £5,288k against budget £4,045k; material forecast risk circa £1.000m
findings.quote: Budgeted savings continue to be stubborn to achieve due to market conditions in rationalising the estate through disposal or redeployment

findings.paper_title: E3717_APPENDIX 1 - Revenue Monitor Commentary
findings.headline: Improving Communications savings of £300k will not fully land in 2026/27, and a £122k Letterbox to Inbox saving has not yet been achieved.
findings.detail: The paper says implementation has taken longer than profiled, with Parking Services due to go live on 1 October 2026 and digital letter delivery from December 2026. It expects most savings to be realised across 2026/27 and 2027/28, and that the full benefits of Letterbox to Inbox will come in 2027/28.
findings.matters: Digital transformation savings slipping across two years is a common pressure in council budgets, and the paper gives specific dates and amounts that peers can compare against their own programmes.
findings.figures: Improving Communications saving £300k not fully in-year; Letterbox to Inbox saving £122k not achieved; Customer Services variance £522k adverse; forecast £3,525k against budget £3,003k
findings.quote: implementation has taken longer than originally profiled and will not deliver the full in-year saving.

findings.paper_title: E3717_APPENDIX 1 - Revenue Monitor Commentary
findings.headline: Roman Baths visitor numbers are 5% below budget, but the service anticipates its highest ever surplus, around £1 million above the 2025/26 outturn.
findings.detail: The paper reports group visits declining, with a forecast income reduction of approximately £1.0m at Q2 partly mitigated by cost savings, corporate hire and planned Q4 price increases. The net variance is £541k adverse, and the service expects private hire and admission yield to offset lower volumes.
findings.matters: Visitor-attraction income is exposed to tourism and travel shocks, and this paper shows a council heritage asset setting a record surplus despite a volume shortfall against budget.
findings.figures: Visitor numbers 5% below budget and 3% below prior year; net surplus budget £13.261m; forecast income reduction approximately £1.0m; variance £541k adverse; surplus around £1 million above 2025/26 outturn
findings.quote: the service anticipates delivering its highest ever surplus, around £1 million above the 2025/26 outturn, albeit below the ambitious budget target set for 2026/27.

findings.paper_title: E3717_APPENDIX 1 - Revenue Monitor Commentary
findings.headline: Housing Delivery Vehicle forecast variance of £625k is attributed to delayed development projects affecting profit and dividend timing, to be met from the Commercial Income Risk Reserve.
findings.detail: The paper links the variance to delays in planned development projects that move the timing of profit generation and dividend payments. It says the reserve will be used based on the actual outturn, and that the position is under review alongside the company's approved Sustain Plan in 2027/28 budget setting.
findings.matters: Council-owned development companies that rely on dividends are a source of scrutiny for finance directors and lenders, and this shows a dividend shortfall being absorbed by a reserve.
findings.figures: Housing Delivery Vehicle forecast variance £625k; budget (£1,000k) dividend income; forecast (£375k)
findings.quote: The Commercial Income Risk Reserve will be used to mitigate the pressure based on the actual outturn position.

findings.paper_title: E3717_APPENDIX 1 - Revenue Monitor Commentary
findings.headline: Capital financing forecast £1,450k favourable, from £750k lower borrowing costs and £700k higher investment interest.
findings.detail: The paper attributes the borrowing saving to lower rates on new and replacement borrowing against budget and a delayed need to borrow because of higher cash balances. The investment saving comes from higher return rates and a higher investment balance than budgeted.
findings.matters: Finance directors and lenders track whether treasury management is producing budget headroom, and this shows borrowing timing and rates driving the saving.
findings.figures: Capital financing variance (£1,450k); borrowing costs favourable £750k; investment interest favourable £700k
findings.quote: There is a £750k favourable forecast in borrowing costs, due to lower rates achieved on new/replacement  borrowing when compared to budgeted rates, and delayed need to borrow due to higher cash balances.

findings.paper_title: E3717_APPENDIX 1 - Revenue Monitor Commentary
findings.headline: Commercial Estate forecast is £1,491k adverse, with Bath Quays South contributing £872k from a lack of tenants.
findings.detail: The paper says rental income is on target, but the net budget position is adverse because of rising Service Supported Borrowing costs as assets join the Void Works programme and the cost of funding two legal advisers. Bath Quays South was transferred into the cashlimit and is cited as the £872k adverse impact.
findings.matters: Commercial property income and void costs are a lending and budget-risk focus, and the paper shows borrowing costs pressuring the revenue position even where rent is on target.
findings.figures: Commercial Estate variance £1,491k adverse; Bath Quays South adverse impact £872k; current budget (£12,181k) net income; forecast (£10,691k)
findings.quote: The Bath Quays South property has been transferred into this cashlimit and that has an adverse impact of £872k from the lack of tenants in the building.

findings.paper_title: E3717_APPENDIX 1 - Revenue Monitor Commentary
findings.headline: Dedicated Schools Grant forecast overspend for 2026/27 is £19.615m, with £46.505m cumulative overspend brought forward, and the DfE's new DSG Stability Grant will support 90% of the cumulative overspend.
findings.detail: The paper states that the Safety Valve programme has been replaced by a DSG Stability Grant, that the SEND reform plan feeding into the grant calculation was submitted in summer 2026 and recently approved, and that the High Needs Block is the main driver.
findings.matters: The 90% support on the cumulative deficit is a specific, dated government funding mechanism that other councils with high-needs deficits will be assessing against their own positions.
findings.figures: DSG forecast overspend 2026/27 £19.615m; 2025/26 final overspend £13.716m; cumulative overspend brought forward £46.505m; stability grant support 90% of cumulative overspend
findings.quote: The Department for Education have replaced the Safety Valve programme with a new DSG Stability Grant which will support 90% of the cumulative overspend.

findings.paper_title: E3717_APPENDIX 1 - Revenue Monitor Commentary
findings.headline: Children, Young People & Families forecasts a £7,008k overspend on a £36,769k budget, driven by £5.9m of residential placement overspend.
findings.detail: The paper attributes the pressure mainly to demand budgets, with residential placements the largest overspend area and staffing pressures of £1.3m from agency use and delayed staffing efficiencies. It also reports that £465k of 2026/27 budgeted savings have been fully delivered.
findings.matters: Placement-led overspends in children's social care are a recurring pressure across English councils, and the paper's split between demand, staffing and savings gives a comparison point for peers.
findings.figures: Forecast overspend £7,008k; budget £36,769k; demand budgets £5.7m; residential placements £5.9m; staffing pressures £1.3m; budgeted savings £465k
findings.quote: The main driver of pressure is £5.7m Demand Budgets, with Residential placements being the main area of overspend at £5.9m.

findings.paper_title: E3717_APPENDIX 1 - Revenue Monitor Commentary
findings.headline: Council forecasts a £9,062k variance before reserve and contingency actions, reduced to £3,725k after a £2,680k release of budgeted corporate contingency and a £2,657k use of the Commercial Income Risk Reserve.
findings.detail: The paper's council total shows a forecast outturn of £199,942k against a current budget of £190,881k. It then applies a release of budgeted corporate contingency and a use of the Commercial Income Risk Reserve, giving a revised council total forecast of £197,285k against a revised budget of £193,561k.
findings.matters: A finance director at a peer council can compare how much of a service overspend is being met from a dedicated risk reserve versus contingency, which affects the reserve headroom available for 2027/28.
findings.figures: Council total variance £9,062k; release of corporate contingency £2,680k; use of Commercial Income Risk Reserve £2,657k; revised council variance £3,725k; revised budget £193,561k; forecast £197,285k
findings.quote: Revised Council Total 193,561 92,297 197,285 3,725

findings.matters: A finance director can see that the Council's central funding is treated as fixed for the next two years, while the 2027/28 provisional settlement remains unknown.

findings.matters: A council with a low Council Tax base faces a narrower local income option, which affects how other councils assess their own tax-raising room.

findings.detail: The paper lists Fair Funding Reform as the first funding challenge and gives the adverse effect on the Council's central government allocation. It is one of three funding pressures set out in the report's introduction.
findings.matters: Other councils can see how a funding reform is being quantified in a single authority's medium-term plan.
findings.quote: which had an adverse impact on the Council in terms of its

findings.paper_title: E3738_2027_28_MTFS Report
findings.headline: The MTFS shows a remaining funding gap of £14.790m for 2027/28, with projected gaps in each later year to 2031/32 and a five-year total of £38.229m.
findings.detail: The paper says that after updating assumptions the remaining gap for 2027/28 is £14.790m, with gaps of £9.485m, £5.318m, £4.764m and £3.871m in 2028/29 to 2031/32. Officers are working on options to close the gap, which will be consulted on before the February 2027 budget report.
findings.matters: A finance director at another council can compare the size and profile of this gap, and the planned route to close it, with their own five-year position.

findings.paper_title: E3717_APPENDIX 2 - Key Scheme Capital Monitoring Commentary
findings.headline: Commercial Estate Refurbishment Programme has completed works on seven vacated properties, forecasting £3,227k against a £3,227k budget, with each either let or under offer.
findings.detail: The completed works cover 6 Milson Street, 8 Broad Street, 15/16 Broad Street, 18 New Bond Street, 9 Abbey Churchyard, 5 Princes Building and 33 Walcot Street. The paper says all are now let or under offer.
findings.matters: Refurbishment of vacant commercial units being let or put under offer shows the council converting capital spend into rental income, which is directly relevant to income-dependent debt servicing.
findings.figures: Budget £3,227k; forecast £3,227k; variance £0k; re-phasing to future years £0k
findings.quote: which are either now let or under offer.

findings.paper_title: E3717_APPENDIX 2 - Key Scheme Capital Monitoring Commentary
findings.headline: Waste Infrastructure Modernisation forecasts £5,536k against a £6,912k budget and is expected to come in under budget, with completion on both sites due in October 2026.
findings.detail: The new Recycling Centre on Locksbrook Road and co-location of Cleansing Services with the Transport Depot are progressing to programme. The paper says the contingency release will be confirmed in the final settlement of accounts.
findings.matters: A capital scheme forecast to finish under budget with contingency still to be released is a useful reference for other councils budgeting for similar depot and recycling-centre builds.
findings.figures: Budget £6,912k; forecast £5,536k; variance £1,376k; re-phasing to future years £49k
findings.quote: The scheme is expected to come in under budget with release of the contingency to be confirmed in the final settlement of accounts.

findings.paper_title: E3717_APPENDIX 2 - Key Scheme Capital Monitoring Commentary
findings.headline: CRSTS Liveable Neighbourhoods forecasts £3,857k against a £4,517k budget, with two schemes paused and remaining interventions in Sydney Road and Lyme Road moved to 2027.
findings.detail: The paper reports that Southlands, Entry Hill and Chelsea Road have been delivered and Lyme Road/Charmouth Road is in construction. It also records that Pulteney Estates Area and London Road and Snow Hill are paused.
findings.matters: A government-funded programme with paused schemes and slipped delivery dates shows the scheduling and grant-conditions risk that comparable authorities on CRSTS-type funding face.
findings.figures: Budget £4,517k; forecast £3,857k; variance £660k; re-phasing to future years £660k
findings.quote: Two schemes have been paused at this time (Pulteney Estates Area and London Road and Snow Hill).

findings.paper_title: E3717_APPENDIX 2 - Key Scheme Capital Monitoring Commentary
findings.headline: Somer Valley Enterprise Zone infrastructure forecasts £2,407k against a £6,658k budget, with land acquisition now expected to complete in 2027/28.
findings.detail: Land acquisition is required to deliver the scheme. Negotiations and preparations for a potential Compulsory Purchase Order are ongoing, and the paper moves completion into the next financial year.
findings.matters: Land acquisition that depends on a possible compulsory purchase order is a timing risk that other councils with enterprise zone or regeneration land assembly will recognise.
findings.figures: Budget £6,658k; forecast £2,407k; variance £4,251k; re-phasing to future years £4,251k
findings.quote: negotiations and preparations for a potential Compulsory Purchase Order (CPO) ongoing, now expected to complete in 2027/28.

findings.paper_title: E3717_APPENDIX 2 - Key Scheme Capital Monitoring Commentary
findings.headline: Haycombe Crematorium gas cremator replacement forecasts £800k against a £1,473k budget, after investigations identified structural, infrastructure and operational implications.
findings.detail: A Single Member Decision (E3629) approved the replacement in July 2025. The paper says a comprehensive review and options appraisal is now underway, including the option of aligning with proposals to expand Haycombe Cemetery.
findings.matters: A scheme approved by decision that is now being re-scoped, with its cost and programme under review, shows how an approved capital decision can be reopened after site investigation.
findings.figures: Budget £1,473k; forecast £800k; variance £673k; re-phasing to future years £673k
findings.quote: However, investigations identified significant structural, infrastructure and operational implications associated with replacement cremators within the existing building.

findings.paper_title: E3717_APPENDIX 2 - Key Scheme Capital Monitoring Commentary
findings.headline: Commercial Estate Fire Safety Works forecasts £1,427k against a £2,820k budget, with asbestos removal costs and more doors in the programme putting "under pressure" the approved budget.
findings.detail: The paper links the pressure to asbestos removal costs and to lease review conclusions that bring more doors into the programme. The £1,393k variance is shown as re-phased to future years.
findings.matters: A fire safety programme on a commercial estate that is exceeding its approved budget bears on the council's landlord liabilities and on its property income.
findings.figures: Budget £2,820k; forecast £1,427k; variance £1,393k; re-phasing to future years £1,393k
findings.quote: Asbestos removal costs and recent changes to the lease review door conclusions, meaning more doors are now to be included in the programme, combines to continue to put the current approved budget under pressure.

findings.paper_title: E3717_APPENDIX 2 - Key Scheme Capital Monitoring Commentary
findings.headline: Guildhall Roof Refurbishment forecasts £191k of its £3,014k 2026/27 budget, with £2,822k re-phased to future years, after higher than expected estimates led to a reprioritisation exercise.
findings.detail: The paper says the start on site is now June 2027 and works will run for 18 months. It attributes the change to estimates that came in above expectations.
findings.matters: A £2,822k re-phasing on one building shows how a single estimate revision can move a large share of a year's capital programme into later years.
findings.figures: Budget £3,014k; forecast £191k; variance £2,822k; re-phasing to future years £2,822k
findings.quote: Higher than expected estimates are resulting in an reprioritisation exercise.

findings.committee: Corporate Policy Development and Scrutiny Panel
findings.paper_title: Rev & Cap Q2 Monitor PDS Report
findings.headline: The Revenue Budget Contingency Reserve will be used if the forecast overspend cannot be fully mitigated, with replenishment required in future years.
findings.detail: The paper states that if the budget position is not fully mitigated, the reserve would need to be used subject to approval. Replenishment would either increase future savings requirements in the Medium Term Financial Strategy or come from a reserves review.
findings.matters: Drawing on a revenue budget contingency reserve, and the need to replenish it, affects the council's future savings targets and its reserve adequacy, which lenders and peer finance officers track.
findings.figures: None given for the reserve balance or the amount that may be drawn
findings.quote: the Council’s Revenue Budget Contingency Reserve will need to be utilised, subject to approval.

findings.committee: Corporate Policy Development and Scrutiny Panel
findings.paper_title: Rev & Cap Q2 Monitor PDS Report
findings.headline: The 2026/27 Capital Programme is forecast at £122.579m against a £158.077m budget, with £34.055m of the £35.498m variance rephased into future years.
findings.detail: The paper attributes most of the capital variance to rephasing, meaning spend is expected to move into future years rather than being removed from the programme.
findings.matters: A high proportion of capital underspend being rephased rather than saved is a signal for lenders and finance officers about the timing of borrowing and the likely scale of future capital spending.

findings.quote: The current position of the 2026/27 Capital Programme is a forecast of £122.579m against a budget of £158.077m.

findings.committee: Corporate Policy Development and Scrutiny Panel
findings.paper_title: Rev & Cap Q2 Monitor PDS Report
findings.headline: £1.325m (49%) of £2.715m undelivered 2025/26 savings are forecast as achieved, leaving £1.390m mitigated by one-off underspends, delayed or undeliverable.
findings.detail: The paper reports on the prior year's undelivered savings separately from the 2026/27 programme. The balance is being covered through one-off underspends or is delayed or undeliverable.
findings.matters: Carry-forward of undelivered prior-year savings, and reliance on one-off underspends to cover them, is a sign of how durable a council's savings delivery is.

findings.quote: leaving a balance of £1.390m as mitigated by one-off underspends, delayed or undeliverable.

findings.committee: Corporate Policy Development and Scrutiny Panel
findings.paper_title: Rev & Cap Q2 Monitor PDS Report
findings.headline: At Quarter 2, £6.393m (84%) of the £7.638m 2026/27 savings are forecast as delivered, with the remainder mitigated, delayed or flagged as undeliverable.
findings.detail: The paper states that the 2026/27 approved net savings of £7.243m, adjusted for £0.395m of reversals of 2025/26 one-off savings, total £7.638m to be delivered. The remainder is being mitigated through alternative measures, or flagged as delayed or undeliverable.
findings.matters: The share of savings forecast as delivered at mid-year is a direct indicator of whether a council's medium-term savings plan is on track.
findings.figures: £6.393m (84%) forecast delivered; £7.638m total to be delivered; £7.243m approved net savings; £0.395m reversals of 2025/26 one-off savings
findings.quote: At present £6.393m (84%) savings are forecast as delivered

findings.committee: Corporate Policy Development and Scrutiny Panel
findings.paper_title: Rev & Cap Q2 Monitor PDS Report
findings.headline: Lower borrowing costs and treasury management performance are helping offset the adverse financial position, according to the paper.
findings.detail: The paper identifies lower borrowing costs and strong treasury management performance as factors offsetting the overall adverse position. No figure is given for the size of the offset.
findings.matters: A council citing lower borrowing costs as an in-year offset is relevant to lenders and treasury officers at peer councils assessing the same rate environment.
findings.figures: None given in this paper
findings.quote: Lower borrowing costs and strong treasury management performance are also helping offset the adverse financial position.

findings.committee: Corporate Policy Development and Scrutiny Panel
findings.paper_title: Rev & Cap Q2 Monitor PDS Report
findings.headline: A £2.657m drawdown from the Commercial Income Risk Reserve is assumed to offset income shortfalls on the Commercial Estate, Heritage Services and the Housing Delivery Vehicle.
findings.detail: The paper reports that income for these three areas is lower than budgeted and that the shortfall is being mitigated through an assumed reserve drawdown rather than through the budget itself.
findings.matters: Using a dedicated income risk reserve to cover commercial income shortfalls shows how much headroom remains in that reserve and whether commercial income risk is being absorbed by reserves.
findings.figures: £2.657m assumed drawdown from the Commercial Income Risk Reserve
findings.quote: Income is significantly lower than budgeted for the Commercial Estate, Heritage Services and the Housing Delivery Vehicle, however these are being mitigated through an assumed drawdown of £2.657m from the Commercial Income Risk Reserve.

findings.committee: Corporate Policy Development and Scrutiny Panel
findings.paper_title: Rev & Cap Q2 Monitor PDS Report
findings.headline: The £2.680m Corporate Contingency has been fully released at Quarter 2 and is not enough to offset all pressures across the organisation.
findings.detail: The paper states the whole Corporate Contingency has been used to mitigate the forecast pressures, and that the remaining gap is not covered by it.
findings.matters: A fully released contingency means no unallocated headroom remains in-year, which is relevant to any council assessing how much buffer its budget retains.
findings.figures: £2.680m Corporate Contingency, fully released
findings.quote: The budgeted Corporate Contingency of £2.680m has been fully released to mitigate these pressures however, it isn’t sufficient to offset all financial pressures across the organisation.

findings.committee: Corporate Policy Development and Scrutiny Panel
findings.paper_title: Rev & Cap Q2 Monitor PDS Report
findings.headline: Children's Services forecasts a £7.391m pressure, the largest in the council, primarily due to high-cost packages for the most vulnerable and complex young people
findings.detail: The paper names Children's Services as the largest cost pressure, with Corporate Estate, Home to School Transport and Customer Services also forecasting significant pressures. The paper attributes the Children's Services figure primarily to high-cost packages.
findings.matters: Demand-led placement costs in children's services are a known source of overspend, and the scale of this forecast will be compared against peers' own placement pressures.
findings.figures: £7.391m total forecast pressure for Children's Services
findings.quote: Children’s Services are forecasting the largest cost pressure, £7.391m in total, which is primarily due to high-cost packages required to support the most vulnerable and complex young people in the area.

findings.committee: Corporate Policy Development and Scrutiny Panel
findings.paper_title: Rev & Cap Q2 Monitor PDS Report
findings.headline: Quarter 2 forecast General Fund revenue outturn is an adverse net variance of £3.725m, against £5.320m at Quarter 1.
findings.detail: The paper reports that in-year recovery plans have reduced the forecast overspend and that managers continue to prioritise cost control to bring the budget back towards balance before year-end. The Quarter 1 figure was produced on a risk-based approach.
findings.matters: A finance director at another council can compare the Quarter 1 to Quarter 2 movement to judge how quickly in-year recovery plans reduced a forecast overspend.
findings.figures: £3.725m adverse net variance at Quarter 2; £5.320m adverse at Quarter 1
findings.quote: The forecast General Fund revenue budget outturn position as at Quarter 2 is an adverse net variance of £3.725m.

findings.headline: Government to pay £41.938m High Needs Stability Grant on 30 November 2026, leaving £4.567m of the DSG deficit for the council to fund from 2028/29
findings.detail: The DfE approved the council's SEND Reform Plan on 2 October 2026. The paper says the grant is expected to fund 90% of the DSG deficit at the end of 2025/26, and that the council will fund the balance from 2028/29 when the statutory override ends.
findings.matters: A finance director at another council with a DSG deficit can compare the 90% grant share and the residual balance left for the council to fund after the statutory override ends.

findings.committee: Corporate Policy Development and Scrutiny Panel
findings.paper_title: Corporate Strategy Performance Report
findings.headline: Adult social care reviews were up to date for 69% of people against a target of 80%, and the data counting rules are under review.
findings.detail: The paper cites the Care Act section 27 duty to keep care and support plans under review and asks Cabinet to note it. It says the data model is being reviewed, so values may change in future reports.
findings.matters: Reviews are a statutory duty, and a council whose indicator counting rules are changing will have figures that move for reasons unrelated to service delivery.
findings.figures: 69% of people with an up-to-date review; target 80%; -1% change
findings.quote: Proportion of people with an up-to-date Adult Social Care review is 69% vs target 80% ( -1% change).

findings.committee: Corporate Policy Development and Scrutiny Panel
findings.paper_title: Corporate Strategy Performance Report
findings.headline: Children on Education Health & Care Plans total 2,959, up 4%, and the paper expects demand to stay elevated until national SEND reforms take effect.
findings.detail: The paper describes demand as high but in line with previous patterns. It ties the expected elevated level to national SEND reforms and new DfE legislation, with no date given.
findings.matters: EHCP numbers drive high-needs spending, and a finance director would want to know that the council expects demand to stay high until national reform.
findings.figures: 2,959 children on EHCPs; +4% change
findings.quote: Demand remains high but in line with previous patterns and expected to remain elevated until national SEND reforms and new DfE legislation take effect.

findings.committee: Corporate Policy Development and Scrutiny Panel
findings.paper_title: Corporate Strategy Performance Report
findings.headline: Children looked after stood at 66.26 per 10k, up 2%, and above the England average.
findings.detail: The paper says the rise is driven mainly by unaccompanied asylum-seeking children and older adolescents entering care in crisis. It gives no cost figures.
findings.matters: Rising numbers in care are a major driver of children's services spending, and the paper places the council above the England average.
findings.figures: 66.26 children looked after per 10k; +2% change
findings.quote: Children looked after per 10k are 66.26 (+2%), trending upward over recent quarters. Levels are currently above the England average

findings.committee: Corporate Policy Development and Scrutiny Panel
findings.paper_title: Corporate Strategy Performance Report
findings.headline: Households in temporary accommodation stood at 82 against a target of 90, up 19% in the latest quarter.
findings.detail: The paper attributes the rise to families needing accommodation, with demand linked to landlord exits rather than reduced move-on supply. The paper gives no cost figures for temporary accommodation.
findings.matters: Temporary accommodation demand is a recognised budget pressure, and a finance director here or at a peer council would want to know when that demand is rising.
findings.figures: 82 households; target 90 households; +19% change in the latest quarter
findings.quote: Households in temporary accommodation is 82 vs target 90,but has increased +19% in the latest quarter. The increase has been driven by families requiring accommodation, with increased demand linked to landlord exits rather than reduced move-on supply.

findings.detail: The measure excludes the CCLA property fund and the two ESG funds, which are unrated. The paper describes this as a voluntary measure of credit risk.
findings.matters: A portfolio held well above its minimum rating shows how the council's cash exposure to bank and local authority counterparties is managed.
findings.figures: Portfolio average AA+ at 31 March 2026; minimum A-
findings.quote: The Council has adopted a voluntary measure of its exposure to credit risk

findings.paper_title: TREASURY MANAGEMENT OUTTURN 2025/26
findings.headline: 22.49% of borrowing falls due within 12 months, against an upper limit of 30.00%
findings.detail: The maturity structure indicator measures refinancing risk. The paper's table shows the share due in each band, with 8.34% in 24 months to five years and 13.81% in five to ten years.
findings.matters: A large share of debt maturing within a year means frequent refinancing, which is a direct exposure for lenders and for a finance director planning replacement funding.
findings.figures: Under 12 months 22.49% (upper limit 30.00%); 24 months to 5 years 8.34%; 5 to 10 years 13.81%
findings.quote: Under 12 months 30.00 Nil 22.49

findings.paper_title: TREASURY MANAGEMENT OUTTURN 2025/26
findings.headline: The paper projects that actual borrowing will fall below the liability benchmark
findings.detail: At 31 March 2026 borrowing was almost in line with the liability benchmark. The paper says borrowing is projected to fall below it, and the funding gap between the two is offered as a guide to the amount and length of future borrowing.
findings.matters: A council moving from internal borrowing to external borrowing creates new demand in the market, and lenders and finance directors can see from the projected gap that the council expects to need to borrow.
findings.figures: Liability benchmark and actual borrowing are both well below the CFR of £386m at 31 March 2026
findings.quote: Looking forward the actual borrowing will fall below the liability benchmark

findings.paper_title: TREASURY MANAGEMENT OUTTURN 2025/26
findings.headline: The minimum cash available within three months was £18.400m on 30 March 2026, against a prudential indicator of £15.000m
findings.detail: The liquidity indicator measures cash available to meet unexpected payments within a rolling three-month period without additional borrowing. The paper says the £20.000m of borrowing taken in the year was partly to keep this above £15.000m.
findings.matters: The gap between the lowest point and the indicator is the margin a council has before it must borrow to meet unexpected payments, which is worth comparing against peers.
findings.figures: Indicator minimum £15.000m; minimum during year £18.400m on 30-Mar-26
findings.quote: The Council has adopted a voluntary measure of its exposure to liquidity risk

findings.paper_title: TREASURY MANAGEMENT OUTTURN 2025/26
findings.headline: Investments stood at £31.300m on 31 March 2026, down from £48.200m at 31 December 2025 and £32.600m at 31 March 2025
findings.detail: Of the £31.300m, £21.300m was held in notice (instant access) funds and £10.000m in strategic funds. The paper gives the balances but does not explain the fall from December to March.
findings.matters: Cash balances that fall by £16.9m within a quarter are a visible change in the council's liquidity position, and the paper does not say what drove it.
findings.quote: with £21.300m in short term liquid investments

findings.paper_title: TREASURY MANAGEMENT OUTTURN 2025/26
findings.headline: Total borrowing rose from £275.713m to £288.977m in 2025/26 after £90.000m of new loans
findings.detail: The new loans comprised £20.000m for the annual pension contribution prepayment and to keep the liquidity indicator above £15.000m, and £70.000m to replace maturing loans. Annuity principal of £6.736m was repaid over the year, and the Capital Financing Requirement stood at £386m.
findings.matters: A council that takes £90m of new loans in one year, with £70m of it refinancing, is a regular participant in the local authority market, and the repayment and replacement pattern shows lenders how its requirement is funded.
findings.figures: Balance 1 April 2025 £275.713m; new loans £90.000m; maturity repayments (£70.000m); annuity repayments (£6.736m); balance 31 March 2026 £288.977m; CFR £386m
findings.quote: This includes £90.000m of borrowing taken out during

findings.paper_title: TREASURY MANAGEMENT OUTTURN 2025/26
findings.headline: The strategic pooled funds' fair value rose £0.151m in the year to £7.704m, against a historic cost of £10.000m
findings.detail: Gains and losses on the funds go to an unusable reserve under a statutory override. The override has been extended to 31 March 2029 for investments held before 1 April 2024, so losses hit revenue only when holdings are sold or in 2029/30. The Council says it holds a Capital Financing Reserve that could mitigate any revenue impact if the override is removed.
findings.matters: A fund valued well below its historic cost is a latent loss that the override defers, so the timing of the revenue impact depends on the statutory override remaining in place.
findings.figures: Fair value £7,704,433 at 31/03/2026, up from £7,553,072 at 31/03/2025; historic cost £10,000,000; increase £0.151m
findings.quote: a small increase of £0.151m in the value of

findings.paper_title: TREASURY MANAGEMENT OUTTURN 2025/26
findings.headline: Strategic investments earned 4.18% in 2025/26 against a budgeted return of 4.25%, and the paper gives two different shortfalls
findings.detail: Paragraph 3.14 and Appendix 3 state the shortfall as 0.07%, which matches 4.25% less 4.18%. Paragraph 3.3 gives it as 0.17% below budget, so the paper is internally inconsistent on this figure.
findings.matters: Strategic fund income is a budgeted revenue line, and a finance director needs the correct shortfall before judging whether the income assumption needs to change.
findings.figures: Strategic return 4.18%; budgeted return 4.25%; shortfall stated as 0.07% (paras 3.14, Appendix 3) and 0.17% (para 3.3); 2024/25 return 4.25%
findings.quote: Strategic funds earned a return of 4.18% which is

findings.paper_title: TREASURY MANAGEMENT OUTTURN 2025/26
findings.headline: Operational investments earned an average 4.03% in 2025/26, 0.07% above the 7-day SONIA benchmark of 3.96%
findings.detail: The return was 0.03% above the budgeted rate of 4.00%. The paper's comparison table shows the 2024/25 average for operational investments as 4.97%, so the earned rate fell over the year as Bank Rate was cut.
findings.matters: Earning above benchmark on short-term cash is a good result, but the fall from 4.97% to 4.03% shows how quickly income on cash balances can change with rates.
findings.figures: 2025/26 average 4.03% against SONIA benchmark 3.96% (0.07% above); budget 4.00%; 2024/25 average 4.97%
findings.quote: 4.03% from Operational investments

findings.paper_title: TREASURY MANAGEMENT OUTTURN 2025/26
findings.headline: Interest and capital financing costs for 2025/26 were £2.087m under budget
findings.detail: The paper attributes the underspend to lower rates achieved on new borrowing than budgeted, higher earnings on investments, and a lower Minimum Revenue Provision charge reflecting the rephasing of capital projects. The Revenue & Capital Outturn report to Cabinet on 2 July 2026 carries the variance.
findings.matters: Part of the underspend comes from capital rephasing rather than from a permanent saving, so other councils budgeting for similar MRP and borrowing assumptions can see how much of a favourable variance is timing.
findings.figures: Budgeted £3.699m; actual £1.612m; variance (2.087) FAV. Debt costs (1.309) FAV; MRP (0.181) FAV; interest on balances (0.588) FAV
findings.quote: was £2.087m under budget

findings.paper_title: TREASURY MANAGEMENT OUTTURN 2025/26
findings.headline: Two KBC Bank N.V. LOBO loans of £5,000,000 each are shown as still outstanding at 4.50% after reverting to a variable rate at the end of their fixed periods
findings.detail: The footnote to the borrowing portfolio says all LOBOs have reached the end of their fixed interest period and reverted to a variable rate of 4.50%. The lender may change the rate at six-monthly intervals, and if it does, the borrower may repay without penalty. The paper does not say the lender has exercised that option, and both loans appear in the 31 March 2026 balances with an end date of 08/10/2054.
findings.matters: A LOBO still held after its fixed period is an open rate-reset exposure, and a finance director or lender needs to know whether a call has been exercised and what replacement funding would cost.
findings.figures: KBC Bank N.V. £5,000,000 and £5,000,000 outstanding at 31 March 2026; interest rate 4.50%; end date 08/10/2054
findings.quote: All LOBO’s have reached the end of their fixed interest period and have reverted to the variable rate of 4.50%.
