findings.headline: Two of the five 2024/25 audit recommendations are reported as complete, and the journal approval recommendation has been raised again.
findings.detail: The depreciation recommendation was closed after one asset that had become operational was not depreciated, causing a £470k understatement, and the journal posting access recommendation was closed. The journal approval, accruals and disclosure recommendations remain incomplete.

findings.paper_url: https://democracy.bathnes.gov.uk/documents/s94257/9z Audit Findings Reports UPDATED Audited Statemenet of Account 202526 Appendix 1.pdf
findings.headline: £7.596m of CIL and S38 payments held in creditors has been reclassified from short-term to long-term.
findings.detail: The auditor accepted that the balances relate to projects not yet started, but found management could not demonstrate the Code criteria for short-term classification. The balances have been moved to long-term creditors in the adjusted misstatements.

findings.paper_title: 9z Audit Findings Reports UPDATED & Audited Statemenet of Account 202526 Appendix 1 , item 9.
findings.paper_url: https://democracy.bathnes.gov.uk/documents/s94257/9z Audit Findings Reports UPDATED Audited Statemenet of Account 202526 Appendix 1.pdf
findings.headline: The audit closure certificate will be delayed because the 2023-24 audit remains open following an objection to the financial statements.
findings.detail: The auditor will not certify closure of the 2025-26 audit in its report because of the 2023-24 objection. Confirmation from the National Audit Office on the Whole of Government Accounts is also outstanding, and the pension fund opinion has not yet been issued.
findings.matters: A prior-year objection still open at the next year's audit closure is unusual enough that other councils and lenders will want to know its status.
findings.figures: Delay relates to the 2023-24 audit certificate; no monetary figure given.
findings.quote: We intend to delay the certification of the closure of the 2025-26 audit of Bath and North East Somerset Council in the audit report due to the 2023-24 audit certificate remaining open as a result of an objection to the financial statements.

findings.paper_title: 9z Audit Findings Reports UPDATED & Audited Statemenet of Account 202526 Appendix 1 , item 9.
findings.paper_url: https://democracy.bathnes.gov.uk/documents/s94257/9z Audit Findings Reports UPDATED Audited Statemenet of Account 202526 Appendix 1.pdf
findings.headline: City centre car parks have not been indexed in the 2025/26 revaluation, a departure from the Code that the auditor considers immaterial.
findings.detail: Management judged there is no suitable index for city centre car parks, and the auditor's reasonableness check found a £2.2m variance. The auditor says this is a departure from the Code but is satisfied the assets are not materially misstated, and the Council will review its use of indexation for 2026/27.
findings.matters: Other councils applying the new indexation requirement for the first time will want to see how an auditor treated a non-indexed asset class.
findings.figures: Variance of £2.2m (£2.185m in the body); £99m of assets without a suitable index, including the Roman Baths (£48m).
findings.quote: Management have not indexed city centre car parks as they have assessed there is not suitable index.

findings.paper_title: 9z Audit Findings Reports UPDATED & Audited Statemenet of Account 202526 Appendix 1 , item 9.
findings.paper_url: https://democracy.bathnes.gov.uk/documents/s94257/9z Audit Findings Reports UPDATED Audited Statemenet of Account 202526 Appendix 1.pdf
findings.headline: The Bath Riverside project's split between additions and REFCUS has been corrected, moving £1,041k out of additions.
findings.detail: The Council part-funds Bath Riverside through Homes England funding, but the project does not create a Council balance sheet asset. Recalculating the split found additions understated and REFCUS overstated by £1,041k, which is one of three adjustments the auditor has identified.
findings.matters: Partner-funded regeneration spend split between capital and revenue is a classification issue other councils with joint projects will need to get right.
findings.figures: £1,041k understatement of additions and matching overstatement of REFCUS; £14,536k journal selected in samples; three adjustments totalling £1,041k.
findings.quote: We have recalculated the split and have confirmed that additions have been understated by £1,041k and REFCUS similarly overstated by the same amount.

findings.paper_title: 9z Audit Findings Reports UPDATED & Audited Statemenet of Account 202526 Appendix 1 , item 9.
findings.paper_url: https://democracy.bathnes.gov.uk/documents/s94257/9z Audit Findings Reports UPDATED Audited Statemenet of Account 202526 Appendix 1.pdf
findings.headline: Financial Liabilities at Amortised Cost – Loans was disclosed at £267,164k and has been corrected to £234,164k.
findings.detail: The auditor found the figure in the financial instruments disclosure had been overstated during reconciliation and review, and it was recalculated independently. The Council has adjusted the disclosure, and a reconciliation of liabilities arising from financing activities, which had been omitted, has been added.
findings.matters: A £33,000k difference in the reported loan balance is material to any reader comparing the Council's debt with its own or other councils' disclosures.
findings.figures: Presented as £267,164k; correct amount £234,164k.

findings.figures: £223m PWLB borrowings; £9.1m principal maturing in 2026/27; £9,070k principal and £2,355k accrued interest; £11,425k reclassified from long term to short term borrowing.

findings.paper_title: AUDIT FINDINGS REPORT FOR COUNCIL & AVON PENSION FUND AND AUDITED STATEMENT OF ACCOUNTS 2025/26

findings.headline: Avon Pension Fund expects a net cash outflow of £62.0m over the 12 months from signing, against £264.5m held in highly liquid assets.
findings.detail: Expected payments are £272.6m against expected contributions of £210.0m. The paper also reports 99.99% of contributions received on time for the quarter ending 31 March 2026 and a further £2.0bn in listed equity assets.
findings.matters: The liquidity cover and contribution timeliness show whether the Fund can meet its payments without selling long-term assets, which a lender or peer council would want to know.

findings.paper_title: AUDIT FINDINGS REPORT FOR COUNCIL & AVON PENSION FUND AND AUDITED STATEMENT OF ACCOUNTS 2025/26
findings.paper_url: https://democracy.bathnes.gov.uk/documents/s94108/9 Audit Findings Reports Audited Statement of Accounts 202526.pdf

findings.headline: The Collection Fund outturn was £0.240m worse than estimated, mainly because of a higher Council Tax bad debt provision.

findings.paper_title: 9z Audit Findings Reports & Audited Statement of Accounts 202526 Appendix 3 , item 9.
findings.paper_url: https://democracy.bathnes.gov.uk/documents/s94111/9z Audit Findings Reports Audited Statement of Accounts 202526 Appendix 3.pdf
findings.headline: Core Spending Power is set to rise 8.4% across 2026/27 to 2028/29, against a 15.5% England average for the same period.
findings.detail: The paper says the Council is the fourth lowest funded unitary authority per head in 2026/27. It attributes the gap to the negative impact of the Fair Funding changes.
findings.matters: Relative funding per head is the comparison peers and lenders use to judge a council's revenue base after the Fair Funding reforms.
findings.figures: Core Spending Power £198.59m (2025/26) rising to £215.17m (2028/29); cumulative change 8.4%; England average 15.5%.
findings.quote: 8.4%, well below the England average and reflecting the negative impact of the Fair Funding changes.

findings.paper_title: 9z Audit Findings Reports & Audited Statement of Accounts 202526 Appendix 3 , item 9.
findings.paper_url: https://democracy.bathnes.gov.uk/documents/s94111/9z Audit Findings Reports Audited Statement of Accounts 202526 Appendix 3.pdf
findings.headline: Heritage Services income target was missed, with the Economic and Cultural Sustainable Development portfolio £3.990m over budget.
findings.detail: The paper says visitor numbers were below budget, with the largest shortfalls in months with peak pricing. It also cites delays in renting space at Bath Quays South and in the corporate landlord model, and a £0.665m pressure to be funded from the Commercial Income Risk Reserve.
findings.matters: An income target built on peak pricing that did not hold is a risk other councils running commercial heritage or visitor income will recognise.
findings.figures: Portfolio over budget £3.990m; one-off restructuring costs £2.454m; Corporate Estate and Regeneration £1.593m adverse; Bath Quays South pressure £0.665m.
findings.quote: visitor numbers were lower than budgeted, with larger visitor shortfalls crucially happening during months with peak pricing periods.

findings.paper_title: 9z Audit Findings Reports & Audited Statement of Accounts 202526 Appendix 3 , item 9.
findings.paper_url: https://democracy.bathnes.gov.uk/documents/s94111/9z Audit Findings Reports Audited Statement of Accounts 202526 Appendix 3.pdf
findings.headline: The 2026/27 capital programme plans borrowing of £83.632m, rising to £100.911m in 2027/28.
findings.detail: The paper's funding table shows borrowing as the largest source in 2026/27 and 2027/28 alongside grants. Total schemes are £210.599m in 2026/27 and £142.188m in 2027/28.
findings.matters: A borrowing requirement at this scale, rising in 2027/28, is what lenders will price and what peers will compare against their own programmes.

findings.paper_title: 9z Audit Findings Reports & Audited Statement of Accounts 202526 Appendix 3 , item 9.
findings.paper_url: https://democracy.bathnes.gov.uk/documents/s94111/9z Audit Findings Reports Audited Statement of Accounts 202526 Appendix 3.pdf
findings.headline: Capital spend in 2025/26 was £77.8m, 80% of the revised capital budget, with the shortfall attributed to project timing.
findings.detail: The paper says the underspend mainly reflects delivery time moving projects into future periods. Transfers of £7.273m moved from assets under construction to operational assets in the year.
findings.matters: Slippage against a revised capital budget is a delivery signal for a council planning £210.599m of schemes in 2026/27.
findings.figures: Capital expenditure £77.8m (£77,826k); 80% of revised budget; transfers from assets under construction £7.273m.
findings.quote: Overall capital spending was 80% of the revised capital budget

findings.paper_title: 9z Audit Findings Reports & Audited Statement of Accounts 202526 Appendix 3 , item 9.
findings.paper_url: https://democracy.bathnes.gov.uk/documents/s94111/9z Audit Findings Reports Audited Statement of Accounts 202526 Appendix 3.pdf
findings.headline: Corporate Budgets finished £3.469m under budget, with favourable interest rates on borrowing and cash balances worth £1.906m.
findings.detail: The paper also reports £1.342m less borrowing needed in-year because some corporately supported capital spend was reprofiled, which reduced MRP by £0.181m.
findings.matters: Interest rate and reprofiling effects are a direct offset to the overspends elsewhere, and a finance director will want to see how much of the position they explain.
findings.figures: Corporate Budgets under budget £3.469m; interest benefit £1.906m; reduced borrowing £1.342m; lower MRP £0.181m.
findings.quote: Interest rates have been favourable when compared to what was expected at budget setting on both borrowing and cash balances, resulting in a £1.906m benefit to the Council.

findings.paper_title: 9z Audit Findings Reports & Audited Statement of Accounts 202526 Appendix 3 , item 9.
findings.paper_url: https://democracy.bathnes.gov.uk/documents/s94111/9z Audit Findings Reports Audited Statement of Accounts 202526 Appendix 3.pdf
findings.headline: The Being Our Best savings target of £2.479m was not delivered in 2025/26, and £2.209m carries into 2026/27.
findings.detail: The Resources portfolio was £10.542m under budget overall, but the paper reports a £4.199m overspend on the Savings and Pay and Grading Review, with a £1.721m draw on the Job Evaluation and Pay Structure reserve. The 2026/27 savings target was reduced by £0.270m before the residual was allocated to services.
findings.matters: A pay and grading review that exceeds budget and carries a savings target forward is a pattern other councils running similar reviews will want to compare against.
findings.figures: Savings target £2.479m not delivered; reduced by £0.270m; residual £2.209m carried forward; Savings and Pay & Grading Review over budget by £4.199m; reserve use £1.721m.
findings.quote: The Savings target relating to the Being our Best Programme in 2025/26 of £2.479m has not been delivered in year.

findings.paper_title: 9z Audit Findings Reports & Audited Statement of Accounts 202526 Appendix 3 , item 9.
findings.paper_url: https://democracy.bathnes.gov.uk/documents/s94111/9z Audit Findings Reports Audited Statement of Accounts 202526 Appendix 3.pdf
findings.headline: 65% (£9.15m) of the 2025/26 approved savings of £14.01m were delivered in full, 15% (£2.04m) were mitigated elsewhere, and 20% (£2.82m) were delayed or addressed through budget setting.
findings.detail: The paper describes the Council as having a good track record in savings delivery. The residual savings from the Being Our Best programme were carried into 2026/27.
findings.matters: Savings delivery rates are what lenders and peers test when judging whether a council's budget plan is credible.
findings.figures: Approved savings £14.01m; delivered in full £9.15m (65%); mitigated £2.04m (15%); delayed or addressed £2.82m (20%).
findings.quote: 65% (£9.15m) have been delivered in full, 15% (£2.04m) have been mitigated through savings

findings.paper_title: 9z Audit Findings Reports & Audited Statement of Accounts 202526 Appendix 3 , item 9.
findings.paper_url: https://democracy.bathnes.gov.uk/documents/s94111/9z Audit Findings Reports Audited Statement of Accounts 202526 Appendix 3.pdf
findings.headline: The uncommitted General Fund balance stands at £12.584m after reserve transfers and carry forwards.

findings.matters: The unearmarked balance is the cushion against the DSG and budget pressures the paper describes, so its level relative to the target range is what peers will compare.
findings.figures: Uncommitted General Fund balance £12.584m; schools balances £1.733m, down £0.142m.
findings.quote: remains at £12.584m, which is in accordance with the risk assessed target range

findings.paper_title: 9z Audit Findings Reports & Audited Statement of Accounts 202526 Appendix 3 , item 9.
findings.paper_url: https://democracy.bathnes.gov.uk/documents/s94111/9z Audit Findings Reports Audited Statement of Accounts 202526 Appendix 3.pdf
findings.headline: The 2025/26 General Fund outturn was an overspend of £2.631m after carry forwards, covered by £2.631m of earmarked reserve transfers.
findings.detail: The paper says the overspend was met by proposed transfers of £1.176mm from the Commercial Risk Reserve and £1.455m from the Corporate Revenue Budget Contingency earmarked reserve. Corporate contingencies of £9.830m were released in-year to offset service pressures.
findings.matters: A finance director will want to see how an overspend was met, and here the reserve transfers and the full release of contingency are the mechanisms.

findings.paper_title: 9z Audit Findings Reports & Audited Statement of Accounts 202526 Appendix 3 , item 9.

findings.headline: Children's Services closed 2025/26 £10.181m over budget, driven by residential placements.
findings.detail: The paper says the overspend came after delivery of £2.473m of budgeted savings, and that the residential placements pressure totalled £8.107m across 2024/25 and 2025/26. It also includes £0.840m of 2024/25 invoices to be written off with no prospect of recovery.
findings.matters: Placement costs are a demand pressure many councils report, and the paper gives the placement cost, write-off and savings figures together.

findings.quote: Children's Services - over budget by £10.182m

findings.paper_title: 9z Audit Findings Reports & Audited Statement of Accounts 202526 Appendix 3 , item 9.
findings.paper_url: https://democracy.bathnes.gov.uk/documents/s94111/9z Audit Findings Reports Audited Statement of Accounts 202526 Appendix 3.pdf
findings.headline: The Council expects a High Needs Stability Grant of £41.931m against the DSG accumulated deficit, leaving a residual £4.573m to be funded from 2028/29.
findings.detail: The grant is payable in Autumn 2026 if the Council's SEND reform plan, due to the DfE by 19 June 2026, is approved. The paper says the DfE has not set out how it will fund deficits arising in 2026/27 and 2027/28.
findings.matters: The size of the residual gap, and what happens to the 2026/27 and 2027/28 deficits, is the open question for the Council's General Fund after the override ends.

findings.quote: leaving a residual gap of £4.573m to be funded by the Council from 2028/29 when the Statutory override will end.

findings.paper_title: 9z Audit Findings Reports & Audited Statement of Accounts 202526 Appendix 3 , item 9.
findings.paper_url: https://democracy.bathnes.gov.uk/documents/s94111/9z Audit Findings Reports Audited Statement of Accounts 202526 Appendix 3.pdf
findings.headline: The Dedicated Schools Grant accumulated overspend carried forward into 2026/27 is £46.505m, moved into an unusable reserve under the statutory override that runs to 31 March 2028.
findings.detail: The centrally held DSG overspend for 2025/26 was £13.716m, added to a brought-forward deficit of £32.789m. The paper says the Council cannot fund this from its General Fund unless the Secretary of State gives permission, and the sum has been transferred to the Dedicated Schools Grant Adjustment Account.
findings.matters: A finance director, here or elsewhere, needs to know the size of the SEND deficit and the date after which the statutory override stops protecting the General Fund.
findings.figures: In-year DSG overspend £13.716m; brought-forward accumulated deficit £32.789m; total carried forward into 2026/27 £46.505m; override covers the period to 31st March 2028.
findings.quote: Year-end budgets have been adjusted to reflect the transfer of the £46.505m overspend into a specific unusable reserve for recovery against future DSG funding.

findings.paper_title: 9z Audit Findings Reports & audited Statement of Accounts 202526 Appendix 2 , item 9.

findings.detail: The note departs from the CIPFA example accounts and is recorded as an unadjusted disclosure misstatement with no effect on recognised amounts. The auditor considers the note otherwise clear and sufficient.

findings.figures: Note 20; no impact on recognised amounts

findings.paper_title: 9z Audit Findings Reports & audited Statement of Accounts 202526 Appendix 2 , item 9.

findings.headline: Audit queries now go directly to individual fund managers rather than through Brunel after the move to LPPI from 1 April 2026
findings.detail: The Fund moved from Brunel to LPPI, and pooled-asset audit queries transferred with it. The audit now needs direct correspondence with each fund manager, and in some cases used client portals because responses were slow.

findings.figures: Transition effective 1 April 2026
findings.quote: We have been asked to direct our queries and requests directly to individual fund managers, rather than through Brunel, as was the case in previous audits.

findings.detail: The sampled new user had roles exceeding those requested. Management removed the access after the auditor's enquiry, and the auditor found no journals posted by that user. Management says the error was human, and it will consider adding role reviews to its Agresso user audit.

findings.headline: The 2025/26 CIPFA Code change requires an index for land and buildings not revalued in the year, and the council has disclosed which indices it used.
findings.detail: The letter says the council evaluated its estimation process for land and buildings not revalued in the year after the change to the 2025/26 Code. findings.matters: Any council carrying non-revalued land and buildings under the same Code will have to make the same index-based assessment, so peers will want to see how this one handled it.
findings.figures: None given in the paper.
findings.quote: where no appropriate index is available the reasoning for this assessment

findings.headline: Five investment property assets identified on balance sheet that had been disposed but remained fully depreciated

findings.matters: Demonstrates asset register controls are not robust; investment properties total £231.888m on balance sheet, so control gaps raise concerns about completeness and accuracy of property asset accounting.

findings.headline: £7.6m Community Infrastructure Levy and S38 contributions reclassified from short-term to long-term creditors
findings.detail: Testing identified that £7.596m of CIL and S38 payments were incorrectly classified as short-term creditors. Council could not demonstrate that accounting code criteria for short-term classification had been met (e.g., settlement within 12 months). Reclassification to long-term creditors required.
findings.matters: Proper liability classification affects working capital and creditor assessment; error indicates insufficient review of balance sheet classifications against accounting standards.

findings.paper_title: 9z Audit Findings Reports UPDATED & Audited Statemenet of Account 202526 Appendix 1
findings.headline: Journal approval process lacks formal authorization for transactions under £500k, repeat finding from prior audit
findings.detail: No formal approval process exists for journals under £500k threshold; assurance is taken from retrospective review of sample journals on monthly basis. Journals above £500k are approved but lack documented audit trail. This was also flagged in 2024/25 audit. New financial system with journal authorization process planned for November 2026.
findings.matters: Lack of formal controls over journal posting increases fraud and error risk; repeat finding suggests slow remediation; improved system will strengthen controls but interim period extends exposure.
findings.figures: £500k threshold for formal approval
findings.quote: As in previous years we note that no formal approval process exists for those journals under £500k and assurance is taken from review of a sample of journals, below this threshold, on a monthly basis.

findings.paper_title: 9z Audit Findings Reports UPDATED & Audited Statemenet of Account 202526 Appendix 1
findings.headline: £1.041m reclassification between Additions and REFCUS for Bath Riverside project
findings.detail: Council's allocation of Bath Riverside project expenditure between capital additions and Revenue Expenditure Financed by Capital under Statute was incorrect. Auditor recalculation identified that additions were understated by £1,041k with corresponding REFCUS overstatement due to incorrect application of the funding split ratio.
findings.matters: Accurate capital accounting affects asset reporting and revenue impact measurement; material misclassification between additions and REFCUS indicates control weakness in project accounting.
findings.figures: £1,041k adjustment (additions understated, REFCUS overstated)
findings.quote: This is calculated on a specific ratio and recalculation of the split identified that the figures disclosed in the financial statements are incorrect. We have recalculated the split and have confirmed that additions have been understated by £1,041k and REFCUS similarly overstated by the same amount.

findings.paper_title: 9z Audit Findings Reports UPDATED & Audited Statemenet of Account 202526 Appendix 1
findings.headline: £9.1m PWLB principal maturity reclassified from long-term to short-term borrowing
findings.detail: Testing identified that £9.1m of PWLB principal and £2.355m of accrued interest maturing in 2026/27 had not been classified as short-term borrowing. Council holds £223m in PWLB borrowings across a range of horizons. Adjustment made to balance sheet and financial instruments disclosures.
findings.matters: Proper classification of debt maturities is essential for assessing liquidity and refinancing requirements; lenders and peers track near-term repayment obligations closely.
findings.figures: £9.1m principal maturing in 2026/27, £2.355m accrued interest, £223m total PWLB borrowings

findings.headline: Unmodified audit opinion anticipated on 2025/26 financial statements
findings.detail: Auditor plans to issue a clean, unmodified opinion. Audit is substantially complete with three adjustments identified totaling £1,041k net effect on net expenditure, none of which prevents an unqualified opinion.
findings.matters: Clean audit opinion indicates financial statements fairly present the council's position and provide confidence to lenders and stakeholders in the reliability of reported figures.
findings.figures: Three adjustments identified totaling £1,041k
findings.quote: We anticipate issuing an unmodified audit opinion and will update the Audit Committee on the timing of our audit report once our remaining work is concluded.

findings.paper_title: 9z Audit Findings Reports UPDATED & Audited Statemenet of Account 202526 Appendix 1
findings.headline: Dedicated Schools Grant deficit identified as ongoing financial sustainability risk for fifth consecutive year
findings.detail: Auditor's VFM assessment identified a risk of significant weakness in financial sustainability arrangements, reflecting the ongoing pressure of DSG deficit. This is consistent with findings in 2022/23, 2023/24 and 2024/25. Detailed commentary will be in the Auditor's Annual Report.
findings.matters: Sustained DSG deficits signal structural imbalance in high needs provision funding; peers facing similar pressures watch how councils tackle this; lenders assess whether council has a credible plan to address the shortfall.

findings.matters: A strengthening balance sheet indicates improving financial resilience and demonstrates that the council is building asset value faster than it is accumulating debt.

findings.paper_title: 12 Treasury Management Outturn Report 2025-26Sept
findings.headline: Council deliberately funding £97m of capital needs from internal reserves rather than external borrowing, maintaining borrowing below Capital Financing Requirement.
findings.detail: External borrowing of £288.977m is £97.023m below the Capital Financing Requirement of £386m. Council deliberately limits external borrowing because internal cash and reserves can be deployed more cost-effectively than external borrowing, reducing net debt service costs. This strategy demonstrates confidence in reserves position but means borrowing will likely increase materially as internal balances are gradually depleted to fund capital expenditure. Borrowing is almost in line with the calculated Liability Benchmark and projected to fall below it.
findings.matters: Demonstrates significant internal reserves and confident reserve management strategy. Lender should understand sustainability of this approach and project when council may need to return to higher external borrowing if capital spending is front-loaded or revenue pressure emerges.
findings.figures: CFR £386m, borrowing £288.977m, internal funding gap £97.023m; borrowing at 75% of CFR
findings.quote: The difference between the CFR of £386m and the Borrowing Portfolio of £288.977m represents re-investment of the internal balances including reserves, reducing the in -year borrowing costs in excess of the potential investment returns .

findings.paper_title: 12 Treasury Management Outturn Report 2025-26Sept
findings.headline: Liquid investments fell £11.9m from £33.2m to £21.3m while council took £20m additional borrowing to maintain liquidity threshold.
findings.detail: Short-term liquid investments fell from £33.200m at 31 December 2025 to £21.300m at 31 March 2026 as cash was used for capital and revenue operations. Council took £20m new borrowing (beyond £70m for replacing maturities) to cover annual pension contribution prepayment and maintain minimum liquidity above £15m threshold. Council maintained liquidity of £18.400m, only £3.4m above minimum. This reflects strategic use of internal cash where cost-effective while maintaining prudent liquidity buffers.
findings.matters: Significant drawdown in liquid reserves combined with only modest buffer above minimum threshold indicates tighter working capital position than prior year. While this reflects good treasury strategy (using internal balances before external borrowing), it leaves limited headroom for unexpected cash demands.
findings.figures: Liquid investments £33.200m (31 Dec 2025) to £21.300m (31 March 2026); minimum liquidity maintained at £18.400m vs £15.000m threshold; £20m new borrowing taken
findings.quote: This includes £90.000m of borrowing taken out during the year, which breaks down as £20.000m of new loans taken out to cover the annual pension contribution prepayment and to maintain the Council's liquidity indicator above £15.000m, as well as £70.000m of borrowing to replace maturing loans.

findings.paper_title: 12 Treasury Management Outturn Report 2025-26Sept
findings.headline: Interest and capital financing budget delivered £2.087m favourable variance due to lower borrowing rates and higher investment returns than forecasted.
findings.detail: Actual costs of £1.612m came in £2.087m below budget of £3.699m. New borrowing was taken at lower rates than budgeted. Operational investments earned 4.03% (0.07% above SONIA benchmark 3.96% and 0.03% above budget of 4.00%). Minimum Revenue Provision was lower than budgeted due to capital project rephasing. Strategic investments underperformed at 4.18% vs 4.25% budget, but was offset by stronger operational and MRP savings.
findings.matters: Demonstrates effective treasury management and cost control. A council achieving better-than-expected returns on debt and investment management indicates strong market positioning. However, the MRP variance reflects lower-than-expected capital spend which may relate to delivery challenges.
findings.figures: £2.087m favourable variance; operational investment return 4.03% vs 4.00% budget; strategic investment return 4.18% vs 4.25% budget; MRP actual £11.236m vs budgeted £11.417m
findings.quote: This is due to lower borrowing rates achieved on year to date borrowing when compared to budgeted rates , higher interest rates than budgeted earned on investments and a lower than budgeted MRP charge .

findings.paper_title: 12 Treasury Management Outturn Report 2025-26Sept
findings.headline: Council's externally managed strategic investment funds have fallen to £7.704m from £10m historic cost, an unrealized loss of £2.296m.
findings.detail: Three strategic funds (£5m CCLA property fund, £3m FP Foresight infrastructure fund, £2m VT Gravis clean energy fund) have experienced significant valuation declines due to high interest rates, weak growth, rising inflation, and global uncertainty. The property fund has been particularly affected by weakness in retail and secondary office sectors. The council is deferring recognition of these losses via statutory accounting override extending to 31 March 2029. If the override expires without recovery or holdings are sold, revenue impacts will be charged via the Capital Financing Reserve.
findings.matters: Material unrealized losses on the investment portfolio represent a contingent liability to council revenue. A lender needs to understand whether the Capital Financing Reserve is adequate to absorb potential losses if markets do not recover before the statutory override expires in 2029.
findings.figures: Historic cost £10.000m, fair value 31 March 2026 £7.704m (loss of £2.296m); year-on-year improvement of £0.151m from £7.553m at 31 March 2025
findings.quote: In the current economic environment of high interest rates , weak growth, rising inflation and global uncertainty , the value of equity, bonds and property have fallen significantly since the time of investment .

findings.paper_title: 14z Audit Committee Annual Report Appendix 1
findings.headline: Council identified Section 106 planning fund governance deficiencies requiring ongoing remediation.
findings.detail: The council reported on governance improvements to Section 106 fund management, including new processes, systems, and monitoring. However, it acknowledged that "remaining work required to embed sustainable governance and minimise the risk of future fund repayment," indicating the governance problem is not yet fully resolved.
findings.matters: Section 106 mismanagement creates a risk of fund repayment obligations, which would require council expenditure.
findings.quote: The update covered improvements to the management and governance of Section 106 funds, implementation of new processes and systems, strengthened monitoring and reporting arrangements, progress against agreed actions, and the remaining work required to embed sustainable governance and minimise the risk of future fund repayment.

findings.paper_title: 14z Audit Committee Annual Report Appendix 1
findings.headline: Internal audit opinion reached reasonable assurance but identified audits with weak internal controls.
findings.detail: The 2025/26 annual audit opinion was that reasonable assurance could be provided over internal control systems. However, the audit report included descriptions of audits with 'Level 2' opinions—indicating areas where internal controls were considered weak—though this document does not specify which areas.
findings.matters: Control weaknesses increase the risk of undetected errors, losses, or fraud in council systems.
findings.quote: A summary of the work that supported the annual opinion, including a description of audits that had a 'Level 2' opinion and a summary of position of work as at 31st March 2026.

findings.paper_title: 14z Audit Committee Annual Report Appendix 1
findings.headline: Council classified as major local audit for 2025/26, increasing audit stringency and scrutiny.
findings.detail: For 2025/26, the council was elevated to major local audit status (rather than standard audit) because it administers the Avon Pension Fund. This escalation increases regulatory oversight and stricter audit standards, requiring expert auditors and reduced materiality thresholds.
findings.matters: Major audit classification means increased regulatory scrutiny, reduced materiality thresholds, and additional quality reviews—making control failures more likely to be identified and reported.
findings.quote: for 2025/26 the Council has been classed as a major local audit, as a result of being the administering authority for Avon Pension Fund.

findings.paper_title: 14z Audit Committee Annual Report Appendix 1
findings.headline: Council's governance review identified two significant issues: financial pressures and children's services DSG deficit.
findings.detail: The council's mandatory annual governance review for 2024/25 identified two "significant issues": (1) Financial Challenge – Service Demand and Cost Pressures, and (2) Children's Services DSG deficit and Safety Valve Agreement. Both are being tracked by the Audit Committee as requiring action.
findings.matters: Significant issues flagged in the annual governance statement indicate known problems requiring remediation; a DSG deficit under Safety Valve Agreement is a constraint on council spending.
findings.quote: The Committee was advised of the inclusion of two 'significant issues': 1) Financial Challenge – Service Demand and Cost Pressures 2) Children's Services - Dedicated Schools Grant (DSG) deficit and the Safety Valve Agreement

findings.paper_title: 14z Audit Committee Annual Report Appendix 1
findings.headline: One objection to the 2023/24 accounts remains unresolved.
findings.detail: Grant Thornton issued an unqualified opinion on the 2024/25 accounts with no objections, but a single objection to the 2023/24 accounts—audited in 2024—remains open. This indicates a governance or accounting issue that has persisted across two audit cycles.
findings.matters: Unresolved audit objections to prior-year accounts signal persistent accounting or control deficiencies that have not been remediated.
findings.quote: There were no objections to the 2024/25 statement of accounts but there remained one open objection to the 2023/24 accounts

findings.paper_title: 10z External Audit Annual Audit Report Appendix 1
findings.headline: External auditor issued unqualified opinion on financial statements with no statutory recommendations.
findings.detail: Grant Thornton proposes to issue an unqualified opinion on the Council's 2025/26 financial statements and pension fund statements with no material adjustments. The auditor made no written statutory recommendations, court applications, advisory notices, or public interest reports. The Head of Internal Audit's 2025/26 opinion on the Council's control environment was Reasonable.
findings.matters: An unqualified audit opinion with no statutory recommendations provides independent verification that the financial statements are fairly presented and that no material governance failures have been identified, reducing financial reporting risk for lenders.
